2321595.title: PM chairs valedictory session of National Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development
2321595.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs valedictory session of National Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development
Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, PM calls for making Anganwadis as Centres of community participation
PM suggests Universities could adopt nearby Anganwadi Centres and undertake social-impact studies
On women’s safety, PM emphasises on preventive actions through convergence of efforts across various departments
PM calls for greater focus on the health, nutrition and overall development of adolescent girls
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 9:41PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the valedictory session of the two-day National Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development, at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan earlier today.

The Summit, part of the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Prime Minister, brought together Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories for focused deliberations on nutrition and early childhood care, child protection, women’s safety and empowerment, and strengthening delivery of services through greater convergence.

Prime Minister appreciated the intensive deliberations and emphasised the importance of collaborative decision-making between the Centre and States. He suggested that States could take this model further by organising similar Chintan Shivirs at the district level and at Nagar Palika and Mahanagar Palika levels. He also suggested dedicated Chintan Shivirs for Anganwadi Workers to enable them to exchange experiences, innovations and practical solutions from the field.

Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, Prime Minister stressed that an Anganwadi Centre should not function as an isolated institution but become a centre of community participation. He said families living around Anganwadi Centres could also be encouraged to contribute on special occasions by sharing nutritious food, toys and locally relevant items for children.

Prime Minister called for deeper engagement of universities and educational institutions with Anganwadi Centres. Universities could adopt nearby Anganwadi Centres and undertake social-impact studies, creating opportunities for students to contribute while also generating useful insights for improving service delivery. Medical students and NSS and NCC volunteers could similarly be associated with Anganwadi Centres and community initiatives, he said. He also called for greater focus on the health, nutrition and overall development of adolescent girls.

Prime Minister discussed issues concerning women’s safety, he suggested developing age-appropriate modules for children on women’s safety, dignity and empowerment. He also laid emphasis on preventive actions through convergence of efforts across various departments.

Highlighting the close relationship between cleanliness, health and nutrition, Prime Minister called upon Women and Child Development Departments across the country to take active ownership of the Swachhata Abhiyan. He stressed that good health and nutrition begin with cleanliness and that Anganwadi Centres and surrounding communities could become important platforms for promoting this behavioural change.

Prime Minister observed that national movements such as Vocal for Local and One District One Product (ODOP) should be promoted for Women Empowerment. He added that women’s collectives and community institutions could become important partners in strengthening local products, livelihoods and economic empowerment.

Prime Minister emphasised that the Ministry of Women and Child Development and its counterparts in the States are entrusted with responsibilities touching one of the largest and most important segments of society. The children being nurtured in Anganwadi Centres today will become the youth and citizens who build Viksit Bharat.

2321533.title: Bharat 6G Alliance Strengthens Global Partnerships at 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026
2321533.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Bharat 6G Alliance Strengthens Global Partnerships at 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026
Union MoS for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani addresses valedictory session; DoT highlights ESTIC 2026 and its focus on intelligent networks and quantum communication
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026 concluded at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, with a valedictory address by Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. Organised by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) alongside India Mobile Congress 2026, the three-day event brought together global telecom leaders, policymakers, standards organisations, industry, academia and researchers to discuss the roadmap towards IMT-2030 and beyond.

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development is his address congratulated the Bharat 6G Alliance for organizing the two-day 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026 and for inviting over 75 speakers, which included more than 30 international experts.

The Union Minister of State said that India is moving from being one of the world’s largest telecom markets to becoming an important telecom technology nation and our indigenous technology journey has taught us something important: Self-reliance and global collaboration are not opposites. The stronger our capabilities, the stronger the partner we can be to the world. The Union Minister of State highlighted that 6G must not create a new digital divide while we are still closing the old one. Affordability, accessibility and coverage must therefore be design requirements — not afterthoughts and in 6G, connectivity need not end where the tower ends. The integration of terrestrial and satellite networks can take connectivity further — to remote villages, islands, oceans and places that traditional networks struggle to reach. India is ready to test these technologies at scale — and share what we learn with the world. Our national goal is Viksit Bharat — a developed India by 2047, the hundredth year of our independence.

The experts contributed to sessions on 5G-Advanced foundations for 6G, global standards, spectrum and WRC-27, international trials and testbeds, AI-native and sustainable networks, startups and academia, global alliances, and industrial use cases. The Symposium emphasized that global interoperability and inclusive 6G development will depend on collaboration across countries, industry, research institutions and standards bodies.

The Symposium reaffirmed India’s commitment to contributing to global 6G research and standards while building indigenous capabilities and strengthening international partnerships. Its discussions called for coordinated standards development, collaborative research, spectrum harmonization and large-scale testing, with affordability, accessibility, security and sustainability embedded in the design of future networks.

A key outcome was the exchange of five new MoUs with GSMA, one6G, GTI Alliance, 6G Innovation Forum (6G IF) Taiwan and VOICE, strengthening opportunities for international cooperation, joint research, trials and knowledge exchange. B6GA also released ten white papers and reports, including a Progress Report on 6G Joint Principles, reflecting continued work towards a 6G ecosystem that is secure, open, resilient, inclusive and sustainable by design.

During the valedictory session in the presence of the Minister of State for Communications, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) presented a curtain raiser for the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026. The second edition of this national science and technology platform is scheduled from 27–29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and organised by CSIR in collaboration with 12 participating departments/Ministries. Its theme is “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies”.

The three-day Conclave features plenary talks, 9 thematic technical sessions, panel discussions, presentations by science and technology leaders and deep-tech Startups, exhibitions and B2B/B2G connect meetings.

In the 2nd edition of ESTIC 2026 , DoT is identified to led the  thematic session “Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication”, scheduled for 28 October 2026. The session will explore technologies shaping future digital infrastructure and secure communications. It will feature a keynote by Mr. N. G. Subramaniam, Vice President, TCS; presentations by deep-tech entrepreneurs and technology leaders; and a panel discussion with experts from IIT Kanpur, IIT Delhi, HFCL, Reliance Jio and Bharat 6G Alliance, moderated by Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT.

For more details , please visit: www.estic2026.in

About Bharat 6G Alliance

Established in July 2023, Bharat 6G Alliance is an industry-led collaborative platform bringing together telecom service providers, industry, startups, academia and research institutions to advance India’s 6G ambitions. It promotes indigenous research and innovation, intellectual property creation, international standards engagement and partnerships for an affordable, secure, sustainable and globally interoperable 6G ecosystem.

For more details www.bharat6galliance.com

2321523.title: Raksha Mantri Presents SIDM Champion Awards 2026 and Calls for Greater Private Sector Participation, R&D Investment and Enhanced Defence Production Capacity
2321523.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri Presents SIDM Champion Awards 2026 and Calls for Greater Private Sector Participation, R&D Investment and Enhanced Defence Production Capacity
“National security increasingly depends on the country's ability to design, develop, manufacture and control the technologies and equipment required by our Defence Forces”- Shri Rajnath Singh
“Marking a historic milestone, India's defence exports have reached a record ₹38,424 crore in the FY 2025-26, registering growth of over 60% compared with the previous financial year”- RM
“Defence manufacturers must treat expenditure on R&D as an investment that strengthens operational preparedness, improves competitiveness and contributes to national security” said RM
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh presented the SIDM Champion Awards 2026 at the 8th Annual Session of the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) in New Delhi on  October 09, 2026. A total of 15 Champion Awards were presented at the event, recognising organisations for their achievements in indigenous technology development, product innovation, design, import substitution, manufacturing excellence and exports. RM congratulated the awardees for their contributions to indigenous defence manufacturing, technological innovation, design capabilities, import substitution, manufacturing excellence and exports.

Underlining the importance of the session's theme, “Sovereign Capabilities, Contested Frontiers: Accelerating India's Strategic Autonomy in an Era of Disruption,” the RM said that national security increasingly depends on the country's ability to design, develop, manufacture and control the technologies and equipment required by its Defence Forces. He expressed confidence that India's talent pool, young workforce, industrial capabilities and policy support would enable the country to emerge among the world's leading defence manufacturing nations.

The Raksha Mantri acknowledged SIDM's role in strengthening the domestic defence industrial ecosystem and facilitating policy-industry dialogue. He called upon the Indian defence industry to increase private sector participation in defence production, strengthen research and development (R&D), enhance surge and production capacity, and accelerate technological innovation to advance India's strategic autonomy and self-reliance in defence.

Shri Rajnath Singh said that the transformation of India's defence industry from a major importer of defence equipment to a credible and reliable exporter of sophisticated military hardware is a significant achievement. He noted that India's defence exports reached a record ₹38,424 crore in the financial year 2025-26, registering growth of over 60 per cent compared with the previous financial year. He reiterated the target of achieving ₹50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029.

Emphasising the importance of private sector participation, Shri Rajnath Singh recalled his earlier call for increasing the private sector's share in India's total defence production from approximately 24 percent to 50 percent. He said that the private sector's contribution had grown significantly over the past 12 years and urged industry leaders to set progressive milestones to achieve this shared national objective. He assured the industry that the Government would continue to support its growth while maintaining the necessary standards of regulation, safety, quality and accountability.

Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, the Raksha Mantri observed that modern conflicts increasingly depend on technological capabilities, including drones, missiles, air defence systems and rapidly evolving software and communications technologies. “Defence manufacturers must treat expenditure on R&D as an investment that strengthens operational preparedness, improves competitiveness and contributes to national security” said RM.

Referring to Operation Sindoor, RM highlighted the importance of ensuring that domestic manufacturing facilities can rapidly scale up production when required. He urged the industry to develop innovative solutions to expand manufacturing capacity and respond swiftly to changing operational demands.

Established in 2017, SIDM has emerged as a unified platform representing large enterprises, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), startups, academia and foreign original equipment manufacturers. He said that policy reforms introduced by the Government, including the Defence Acquisition Procedure, Defence Procurement Manual, Positive Indigenisation Lists, SRIJAN portal and Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX), were aimed at expanding the capabilities of India's private defence industry.

The event was attended by Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Director General (Acquisition) Shri A. Anbarasu, SIDM Founder President Shri Baba Kalyani, SIDM President Shri Arun Ramchandani, senior government officials, representatives of the Defence Forces, and leaders of Indian and international defence companies.

2321522.title: Union Health Ministry to Observe World Mental Health Day 2026, Reaffirming Commitment to Accessible, Inclusive and People-Centred Mental Healthcare
2321522.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2321522.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry to Observe World Mental Health Day 2026, Reaffirming Commitment to Accessible, Inclusive and People-Centred Mental Healthcare
​​​​​​​Tele-MANAS renders yeoman service in bringing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health support within easy reach of people across India through toll-free helpline 14416
Over 47.75 lakh calls received since launch on 10 October 2022; 53 Tele-MANAS Cells operational across all 36 States and Union Territories
Women account for nearly 44% of recorded caller profiles, reflecting growing access to mental health support through telephone-based counselling
MANN Jaagriti initiative to strengthen community awareness, encourage early help-seeking and address mental health stigma
Mental health services integrated into over 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs; District Mental Health Programme sanctioned for 767 districts
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will observe World Mental Health Day on 10 October 2026, reaffirming the Government of India's commitment to making mental healthcare accessible, affordable, inclusive and people-centred. This year's global theme, “Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change,” underscores the importance of listening to individuals with lived experiences of mental health conditions and ensuring their voices contribute to shaping responsive mental health policies and services.

At the heart of India's efforts to improve access to mental healthcare is Tele MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States), which has emerged as an important pillar of the country's mental healthcare delivery system. Through its national toll-free helpline 14416, Tele-MANAS is providing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health counselling and support, enabling people to seek professional assistance easily, irrespective of their geographical location or socioeconomic background.

Tele-MANAS: Making Mental Health Support Just a Phone Call Away

Launched on 10 October 2022, Tele-MANAS has rendered yeoman service in bridging gaps in access to mental healthcare by bringing timely counselling, emotional support and professional guidance directly to people through a simple telephone call.

Since its launch, Tele MANAS has received 47,75,644 calls, with 53 operational cells across all 36 States and Union Territories, as of October 2026. This extensive reach reflects the growing importance of accessible, technology-enabled mental health services in addressing diverse mental health needs across the country.

Through 14416, individuals experiencing emotional distress, anxiety, stress, sleep-related concerns or other mental health challenges can connect with trained counsellors without having to travel to a healthcare facility for initial support. Available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and supported by multilingual services, the helpline makes it easier for people to seek help at a time and place convenient to them.

The service is particularly significant for people residing in rural, remote and underserved areas, where access to specialised mental healthcare facilities may be limited. By offering a confidential and supportive platform, Tele-MANAS is also helping address hesitation associated with seeking mental health assistance and encouraging individuals to reach out early.

Beyond initial counselling, the programme facilitates access to specialised mental health professionals and appropriate referral services wherever required, helping ensure continuity of care through linkages with the wider public healthcare system.

Growing Public Engagement Reflects the Importance of Accessible Mental Healthcare

The increasing utilisation of Tele-MANAS highlights the importance of having a readily accessible platform where individuals can seek support without fear of stigma or discrimination.

An analysis of 13,35,275 recorded caller profiles indicates that women account for 43.78% (5,84,587) of callers, while men constitute 54.18% (7,23,427). The substantial participation of women highlights the role of telephone-based counselling in providing a convenient and supportive avenue for seeking mental healthcare.

The service has also witnessed significant engagement among young and working-age populations, with individuals aged 18–45 years accounting for 73.2% of recorded caller profiles.

The range of concerns reported by callers, including emotional distress, stress related to examinations, workplaces and relationships, anxiety and sleep disturbances, demonstrates the importance of accessible mental health support in everyday life.

By providing a platform where individuals can speak openly, receive guidance and be connected to appropriate services, Tele-MANAS is contributing to a broader shift towards recognising mental health as an integral part of overall health and well-being.

MANN Jaagriti: Taking Mental Health Awareness to Communities

As part of World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry is also taking forward MANN Jaagriti, a structured community awareness and engagement initiative aimed at strengthening mental health literacy, reducing stigma and encouraging timely help-seeking.

The initiative seeks to move beyond one-time awareness activities by promoting sustained community engagement through schools, colleges, workplaces, health facilities and other community platforms.

Through locally relevant activities, States and Union Territories will encourage open conversations around mental health, promote early identification of mental health concerns and create greater awareness about available services, including Tele-MANAS.

The initiative will also encourage the involvement of healthcare professionals, educators, community workers, youth, families, caregivers, civil society organisations and persons with lived experience of mental health conditions.

By bringing mental health conversations into everyday community settings, MANN Jaagriti aims to foster supportive environments where seeking mental health assistance is recognised as a positive and important step towards well-being.

Strengthening Mental Healthcare from the Community to the District Level

Complementing the reach of Tele-MANAS, the Government of India continues to strengthen mental healthcare services through the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) and the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP).

The DMHP has been sanctioned for implementation in 767 districts, with support extended to States and Union Territories under the National Health Mission. The programme facilitates outpatient care, counselling, psychosocial interventions, medicines, follow-up care, outreach activities and referral services, alongside provisions for inpatient mental healthcare at the district level.

Mental health services have also been integrated into the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package offered through over 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs across the country.

Through these facilities, primary healthcare teams undertake screening and early identification of mental health concerns, provide psychosocial support and follow-up care, and facilitate referrals to higher healthcare facilities wherever necessary.

Together, these initiatives are strengthening a continuum of mental healthcare that connects community awareness, primary healthcare, district-level services and digital counselling platforms.

Towards a More Inclusive and Supportive Mental Healthcare Ecosystem

On World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reiterates that mental healthcare should be within everyone's reach and seeking help should never be a source of hesitation or stigma.

The growing reach of Tele-MANAS, alongside the expansion of community-based and primary mental healthcare services, reflects the Government's continued efforts to build a responsive healthcare system that places the needs, dignity and well-being of individuals at its centre.

Through Tele-MANAS, the Ministry is reinforcing a simple but important message: mental health support need not be distant, difficult or inaccessible. Help is available, and reaching out can begin with a phone call.

The Ministry encourages individuals experiencing mental health concerns, as well as families and caregivers seeking guidance, to make use of the free and confidential services offered through Tele MANAS at 14416, available 24×7 across the country.

Every conversation matters. Every voice deserves to be heard. And mental health support must be accessible to all.

***

SR

2321518.title: Files to Freedom: DEPwD Drives Swachhata, Pendency Reduction and Efficient Governance
2321518.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Files to Freedom: DEPwD Drives Swachhata, Pendency Reduction and Efficient Governance
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is intensifying its efforts under Special Campaign 6 (2–31 October 2026) to reduce pendency, improve record management, free office space and ensure responsible e-waste disposal.

Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), the campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and promote efficient governance. DEPwD has nominated a Nodal Officer and advised its Attached and Subordinate Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies to nominate Nodal Officers and identify pending matters.

Building on Special Campaign 5.0, DEPwD and its organisations digitised and weeded out 11,972 physical files/documents, freed approximately 15,588 square feet of office space, generated ₹14.47 lakh in revenue and conducted 64 cleanliness campaigns during October 2025.

Swachhata and pendency-reduction activities have continued beyond the annual campaign, with progress regularly recorded on the Special Campaign 6 Portal (SCDPM) in accordance with DARPG guidelines.

The current progress recorded on the portal reflects the Department’s ongoing efforts towards effective record management and disposal of pending matters. Against 52 cleanliness campaigns identified for the current phase, 13 have already been conducted. Of the 928 physical files due for review, 172 have been reviewed, while 32 e-files have been put up for review.

The Department is also addressing various categories of references and public grievances as part of its pendency-reduction efforts. The portal records that 154 out of 202 targeted public grievances and 20 out of 43 public grievance appeals have been addressed. Further, 10 out of 55 references from Members of Parliament, 3 out of 8 Parliamentary Assurances, 2 out of 2 JMC References relating to Cabinet Proposals, and 4 out of 6 PMO References have been addressed.

As part of the ongoing Swachhata Special Campaign 6, a cleanliness activity was conducted on 8th October 2026 at the Guest House of Swami Vivekanand National Institute of Rehabilitation Training and Research (SVNIRTAR) and its adjoining areas. The activity focused on maintaining cleanliness, hygiene and sanitation and promoting responsible waste-management practices, contributing to a clean, healthy campus environment.

Special Campaign 6.0 reinforces the twin objectives of Swachhata and good governance by reducing avoidable pendency, improving record management, freeing usable space and ensuring responsible disposal of obsolete material, particularly e-waste. It seeks to transform redundant records and material into opportunities for greater efficiency, accountability and optimal utilisation of public resources.

2321517.title: “Accessibility Cannot Be an Afterthought”: DEPwD Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach to Sugamya Bharat
2321517.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
“Accessibility Cannot Be an Afterthought”: DEPwD Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach to Sugamya Bharat
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

 “Accessibility cannot be an afterthought, nor can it be left to a single department or agency. It requires a concerted effort across all ministries, departments and levels of government, in partnership with civil society.” This was the central message of Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, IAS, Additional Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), as she called for a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to advancing accessibility across India at the consultation “Sugamyata Ka Sankalp” held at the India International Centre, New Delhi.

Emphasising that accessibility cuts across education, healthcare, employment, transport, financial services and public infrastructure, Ms. Nanda stressed that progress in one sector depends on coordinated action across others. She underscored the need for States to accord accessibility the priority it deserves and for all stakeholders to work together to translate the vision of an inclusive and accessible India into reality. Her message reinforced that accessibility must be embedded at the design stage itself, rather than being added on or corrected later.

Organised by DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, in partnership with The Association of People with Disability (APD), India, and in collaboration with Ipsos, the consultation brought together representatives from government, the disability sector, academia, research and civil society to assess the progress of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, identify persistent accessibility gaps and deliberate on priorities for its next phase.

Shri Girish C. Hosur, Joint Secretary, DEPwD, presented the journey and achievements of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, highlighting the Department’s role in leading the initiative and advancing accessibility across public infrastructure, transport and digital services. His presentation provided the context for discussions on consolidating progress and strengthening implementation in the years ahead.

Shri S. Govindaraj, Commissioner, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, emphasised that accessibility is the need of the hour. He highlighted the importance of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan in advancing accessibility across the country and stressed the need to build on the progress achieved so far to address the barriers that continue to affect persons with disabilities.

Welcoming the participants, Mr. Subir Hari Singh,  President, APD, highlighted the importance of bringing together diverse stakeholders to advance accessibility. He emphasised that meaningful progress depends on sustained partnership among government, practitioners, experts and persons with disabilities. He also outlined APD’s mission and its work in the disability sector.

The consultation featured two moderated roundtable discussions led by Ms. Tripti Sharma, Director, Ipsos. The first examined sectoral challenges in the implementation and use of accessibility data, while the second explored approaches to measuring accessibility across sectors and the essential features of a credible and practical measurement framework. The discussions underscored the importance of reliable data and evidence to guide planning, monitor implementation and assess progress.

Participants included representatives from the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Prasar Bharati and the Airports Authority of India. State Commissioners for Persons with Disabilities, representatives of the State Governments of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, and disability-sector leaders from across India participated both in person and online.

Launched in 2015, the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan marked a significant national initiative to advance accessibility in the built environment, transport systems and information and communication technologies. The consultation, held against the backdrop of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, provided an opportunity to reflect on achievements, identify continuing barriers and explore ways to strengthen accessibility standards, implementation and measurement.

In his closing remarks, Mr. Sukanto Aich, Chief Executive Officer, APD, observed that the gathering itself—bringing stakeholders together to learn from one another and commit to collaboration—was a sign of hope for making the vision of Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan a reality.

The consultation reinforced the shared responsibility of governments, institutions, civil society and the disability sector in building an accessible and inclusive India. Its central message was clear: accessibility must move beyond isolated initiatives to become an integral, measurable and coordinated priority across every sector.

2321516.title: INDIAN NAVY SET TO COMMISSION INDIGENOUS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT ‘MANGROL’
2321516.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY SET TO COMMISSION INDIGENOUS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT ‘MANGROL’
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

Mangrol, the third Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) built by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi, is set to be commissioned into the Indian Navy on 12 Oct 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The ceremony will be presided over by VAdm Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. The event will be attended by senior naval and defence officials, representatives from the Ministry of Defence and Cochin Shipyard Limited, veterans and representatives of indigenous weapons and sensor manufacturers.

Named after Mangrol, a coastal town and prominent fishing harbour in Gujarat's Junagadh district, the ship carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Mangrol (M85), a minesweeper that served the Indian Navy until 07 Apr 2004. The naming of the ship continues the Navy's tradition of preserving the legacy of its former warships.

Built with over 80% indigenous content, Mangrol reflects India's growing capabilities in warship design, construction and integration of advanced weapons and sensors. Constructed by CSL under the Government of India’s Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiatives, the ship marks another important step towards self-reliance in defence shipbuilding.

Designed to detect and counter underwater threats in coastal and shallow waters, Mangrol is equipped with modern weapons and sensors, including the Abhay Hull-Mounted Sonar, lightweight torpedoes, an indigenous anti-submarine rocket launcher and the Maareech Advanced Torpedo Decoy System. Powered by three diesel engines with waterjet propulsion, the ship offers high manoeuvrability for operations in shallow waters. It is also capable of undertaking underwater surveillance, Low-Intensity Maritime Operations and mine warfare-related tasks.

Mangrol will strengthen the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal waters where larger warships face operational limitations. The ship can operate alongside maritime patrol aircraft, helicopters and other warships to detect and counter submarine threats. Its induction will enhance the Navy's ability to protect ports, harbours and coastal approaches while supporting wider fleet operations.

Amid growing underwater threats in the evolving maritime security environment, the commissioning of Mangrol marks an important milestone in strengthening the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal waters. The ship's induction also reflects India's growing indigenous shipbuilding capabilities and reinforces the Navy's commitment to operational preparedness and Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

2321512.title: Department of Posts and Blue Dart Express Limited Sign agreement for India Post Parcel services across India
2321512.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Posts and Blue Dart Express Limited Sign agreement for India Post Parcel services across India
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening India’s parcel and logistics ecosystem, the Department of Posts (DoP), Ministry of Communications, and Blue Dart Express Limited have signed an agreement for India Post Parcel services.

The agreement was signed at New Delhi on 9th October 2026 in the presence of senior officials from both organisations.

The partnership aims to leverage the unparalleled reach and trusted delivery network of the Department of Posts along with Blue Dart’s strong presence in India’s logistics sector to provide efficient, reliable and customer-centric parcel delivery solutions across the country.

Key Highlights of the Agreement

  • Nationwide Last Mile Reach: Blue Dart will utilize India Post’s extensive network for parcel delivery services across urban, semi-urban and rural areas, including remote and underserved regions.
  • Comprehensive Delivery Solutions: The services include delivery of prepaid and COD parcels, OTP-based delivery authentication and real-time shipment tracking.
  • Enhanced Customer Experience: The agreement focuses on faster deliveries, improved operational coordination and seamless technology integration for efficient parcel movement and delivery.
  • Support to E-commerce Growth: The collaboration is expected to further strengthen the logistics infrastructure supporting India’s rapidly growing e-commerce sector.

Benefits to Blue Dart Express Limited

Blue Dart will gain access to DoP’s unparalleled network of 1.64 lakh Post Offices spread across the country. This partnership will allow Blue Dart to expand its logistics operations, improve delivery speed and meet the growing demands of India’s e-commerce sector, especially in remote areas.

Benefits to the Department of Posts

For the Department of Posts, the partnership will provide an opportunity to utilise its postal and parcel network for additional business volumes and strengthen its engagement with the organised logistics sector. The collaboration will also enable the Department to benefit from the operational experience and industry practices of a leading express logistics service provider.

About the Department of Posts

The Department of Posts, under the Ministry of Communications, operates the world’s largest postal network with over 1.64 lakh Post Offices across India. It plays a critical role in providing communication, logistics and financial services with a focus on driving e-commerce growth in India.

About Blue Dart Express Limited

Blue Dart Express Limited is an express logistics and distribution company providing delivery and logistics solutions across India. The company has an extensive domestic network and experience in serving businesses across sectors, including e-commerce and time-sensitive express logistics.

2321511.title: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs at IMC 2026; Highlights Role of Young Innovators in Advancing India’s 5G and 6G Vision
2321511.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
  Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs at IMC 2026; Highlights Role of Young Innovators in Advancing India’s 5G and 6G Vision
Union Minister Shri Scindia Awards Winners of the 5G Innovation Hackathon
“100 5G Use Case Labs to Nurture Young Innovators and Develop Solutions for India and the World”: Union Minister Shri Scindia 
Minister Shri Scindia commends officers of DoT on completion of the specialised Capacity Development Programme on Network and Mobile Security, Distributes Certificates and Badges to them
Initiative aims to transform academic research into practical solutions for India’s next-generation telecommunications ecosystem
Discussions cover AI-native networks, intelligent connectivity, scalable 5G use cases, 6G spectrum roadmap, global standardisation and industry-academia collaboration
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia inaugurated the Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs at the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, underscoring the Government of India’s commitment to strengthening indigenous innovation, promoting research and empowering young innovators in the telecommunications sector. Held under the theme “Building Intelligent Networks: Innovations Driving the 5G Advanced and 6G Era,” the workshop aims to foster industry-academia collaboration and accelerate the translation of academic research into practical, technology-driven solutions. The initiative highlights the pivotal role of students, researchers and academic institutions in developing innovative 5G applications and preparing India’s talent ecosystem for next-generation communication technologies.

The workshop also highlighted the importance of bridging the gap between academic research and industry requirements, enabling young talent to contribute to India’s evolving digital and telecommunications landscape. Through these laboratories, students and researchers can explore emerging technologies, experiment with real-world applications and develop solutions with potential benefits across sectors.

“The networks of tomorrow will be imagined not only in exhibition halls but also in our universities, research laboratories and the minds of young innovators. The 100 5G Use Case Labs were established not merely to provide infrastructure, but to nurture innovators capable of developing solutions for India and the world,” said Union Minister Shri Scindia.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, emphasised the importance of nurturing innovation beyond conventional infrastructure development and empowering the country’s academic and research ecosystem to shape the future of telecommunications.

The workshop reaffirmed the Government’s focus on fostering collaboration among academia, industry and research institutions to accelerate technology development, promote indigenous solutions and prepare India’s talent pool for the 5G Advanced and 6G era.

By placing young innovators and academic research at the centre of technological advancement, the initiative supports India’s ambition to emerge as a global hub for telecommunications innovation and contribute to the vision of a technologically empowered and self-reliant nation.

Inaugural session features awards distribution to the winners of the 5G Innovation Hackathon (Edition-2) 2026

Addressing the participants at the One-Day Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs, the Union Minister  Shri Scindia congratulated the winners of 5G Innovation Hackathon (Edition-2) 2026 and 50 finalists for demonstrating the innovative potential of India’s young talent and encouraged all 1,400 participating teams to continue pursuing new ideas and technological solutions.

Distribution of Certificates to DoT officers Capacity Development Programme

Minister Shri Scindia commended the officers of Department of Telecommunications (DoT), who completed the specialised Capacity Development Programme on Network and Mobile Security. This program included prestigious International certifications like CISSP, CEH, PenTest, CySA etc. Recognising successful completion of the program and their role in strengthening the security of India’s digital infrastructure, Union Minister Shri Scindia distributed the Certificates and Badges to the officers.

Emphasising the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, the Union Minister underscored the importance of 5G Advanced, 6G and research laboratories in shaping India’s telecommunications future. The Minister called for collaborative efforts to develop intelligent networks that are designed and built in India and trusted globally, and formally declared the One-Day Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs open.

Secretary, DoT congratulated the participating teams and highlighted that innovation should extend beyond competitions and prototypes to intellectual property creation, entrepreneurship, industry partnerships and commercial deployment.

Building Intelligent Networks for Viksit Bharat 2047

The workshop reinforced the importance of connecting academic research, industry requirements and national technology priorities to accelerate India’s transition from technology adoption to indigenous technology development.

The Department of Telecommunications reiterated its commitment to strengthening research, encouraging entrepreneurship and fostering collaboration among academia, startups and industry to advance India’s capabilities in 5G Advanced, 6G and next-generation telecommunications.

About 100 5G Use Case Labs Strengthen India’s Innovation Ecosystem

In October 2023, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi awarded 100 5G Use Case Labs to academic institutions across the country. Established under a Government initiative with an outlay of ₹97.67 crore, all 100 labs became operational by April 2025.

The initiative aims to strengthen practical learning, promote research and development in 5G technologies, encourage industry-academia collaboration and enable startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to access 5G infrastructure for developing innovative applications.

The initiative has delivered encouraging results. By August 2026, more than 17,400 students had utilised the labs, while 97 institutions were conducting 5G courses with over 21,000 students enrolled. The initiative has contributed to the development of 634 products and use cases, with 158 intellectual property filings and 32 patents granted. The participating institutions have also strengthened partnerships with startups, MSMEs and other academic and research organisations.

About 5G Innovation Hackathon 2026

This year, the Hackathon received more than 1,400 proposals across emerging telecommunications domains, including 5G Advanced, artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), non-terrestrial networks, Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), network slicing and telecommunications security. The 5G Innovation Hackathon has further strengthened the innovation ecosystem established through the 100 5G Use Case Labs initiative.

Of these, 50 teams were selected and supported with seed funding to develop their ideas. As many as 35 teams are showcasing their innovations at IMC 2026, providing an opportunity to demonstrate their solutions, engage with industry stakeholders and explore avenues for further development and commercialisation.

2321499.title: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Participates in Special Campaign 6.0
2321499.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Participates in Special Campaign 6.0
Campaign Focuses on Institutionalising SWACHHATA, Reducing Pendency in Government Offices and Ensuring Effective E-Waste Management
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in collaboration with its attached and subordinate offices, is actively participating in Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd October to 31st October 2026.

The campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and reduce pendency in Government offices, with a focus on improving administrative efficiency and promoting a cleaner and more responsive work environment.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said that prior to the commencement of the implementation phase, the Ministry undertook the necessary preparatory activities during the preparatory phase from 15th to 30th September 2026. The Ministry and its attached and subordinate organisations are now actively implementing the campaign activities, which commenced on 2nd October 2026.

He said this year's campaign places special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of electronic waste (e-waste), in strict adherence to the guidelines of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. The initiative seeks to promote responsible e-waste management practices and strengthen environmental sustainability across Government offices, he added.

As part of the campaign, focused efforts are being undertaken to ensure the timely clearance of pending matters relating to references from Members of Parliament, State Governments and the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), inter-ministerial communications, Parliamentary Assurances, public grievances and appeals received through the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). These efforts are aimed at reducing pendency and strengthening accountability and responsiveness in administrative functioning.

Aligned with the vision of Swachh Bharat and the objective of enhancing citizens' experience with Government offices, the Ministry's attached and subordinate organisations are extending their full cooperation to outdoor cleanliness drives. These activities seek to promote cleanliness in and around Government establishments and encourage the adoption of sustainable practices.

Through the coordinated implementation of Special Campaign 6.0, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is working towards institutionalising cleanliness, ensuring effective waste management and facilitating the timely disposal of pending matters. The campaign will continue until 31st October 2026.

2321498.title: Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, and its subordinate offices observe Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026
2321498.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, and its subordinate offices observe Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, along with its attached and subordinate offices and field formations, is fully geared up to participate in the upcoming Special Campaign 6.0, being conducted across Government of India departments from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign is being spearheaded by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) to further institutionalise Swachhata (cleanliness) and ensure timely and effective disposal of pending references.

As part of the preparatory phase, which commenced on 17th September 2026, all organizations under the Department of Revenue – including the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Enforcement Directorate, Financial Intelligence Unit – India, and others – have undertaken thorough reviews to identify Pending MP/State Government references, Public grievances, Cleanliness campaigns in offices and public-facing areas, Records for digitization & weeding out and Disposal of scrap, e-waste and obsolete items. Each organisation has designated nodal officers to ensure focused action during the implementation phase. Efforts are underway to sensitise staff and ensure enthusiastic participation at all levels. The Department is also emphasising the use of technology to reduce physical records, promote paperless work environments, and enhance citizen-centric service delivery.

The Department of Revenue had actively participated in Special Campaign 5.0, significantly contributing to the reduction of pendency and promoting a culture of cleanliness. During the period from December 2025 to August, 2026, the Department of Revenue disposed of a total of 65 Inter-Ministerial Reference (Cabinet Notes, CoS Note, EFC Memo etc.), more than 100 VIP references, 12611 Public Grievances, 274 Public Grievances Appeal.

Furthermore, with the scrap disposal, revenue of Rs. 5,03,500/- was also generated.

Special Campaign 6.0 reaffirms the Department of Revenue's commitment to overall cleanliness, e-waste disposal, space management, transparency, and accountability to further enhance administrative efficiency and cleanliness across all levels.

2321480.title: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates AI for Good Lab Workshop at India Mobile Congress 2026
2321480.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates AI for Good Lab Workshop at India Mobile Congress 2026
"The True Measure of AI Will Not Be Model Size, But the Number of Lives It Improves": Union Minister Shri Scindia
India Partners as Pilot Country with ITU to Bridge the Gap between AI Strategy and Impact Across the Global South
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia inaugurated "AI for Good Lab Workshop: From Strategy to Impact," organized jointly by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) at the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi. The landmark event marked a major milestone in transitioning artificial intelligence from global strategy discussions to practical deployment, local solutions, and human-centric scale. The workshop gathered key international dignitaries, including Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director of the ITU Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications along with distinguished researchers, innovators, industry leaders, and policy experts.

Addressing the gathering, the Union Minister Shri Scindia stated, “The journey of the AI for Good Lab from Geneva to New Delhi mirrors the journey that artificial intelligence itself must make—from global conversations to local solutions, from technological possibility to human impact, and from strategy to scale. The distance between AI ambition and AI impact is bridged by skills, compute, data, institutions, and connectivity. Ultimately, the true measure of artificial intelligence will not be the size of its models or the sophistication of its algorithms, but the number of human lives it improves.”

The Union Minister reiterated India's guiding philosophy of "Sarvajan Hitaya, Sarvajan Sukhaya" (for the welfare of all, for the happiness of all), noting that while nearly 2.2 billion people worldwide remain offline, technology must expand human opportunity rather than concentrate it, ensuring the digital divide does not morph into an AI divide.

During the address, the Minister detailed key milestones driving India's domestic AI capabilities and digital infrastructure under the ₹10,000-crore-plus IndiaAI Mission. On the compute infrastructure front, more than 38,000 high-end GPUs have been onboarded at approximately one-third of the global average cost, with an additional 20,000 GPUs being added. In terms of open data and talent, the AI Kosh platform is unlocking datasets and sovereign models across agriculture, healthcare, and education. India currently ranks first globally in relative AI skill penetration, with Indian developers contributing approximately 5.2% of open-source AI projects on GitHub with ten or more stars. Furthermore, telecom innovation is being paired with trust through AI and data analytics tools like Sanchar Saathi, which has facilitated the disconnection of over 7.14 crore fraudulent mobile connections, traced over 35 lakh lost handsets, and prevented potential financial fraud worth over ₹5,000 crore. To support standardization, India's Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC) has developed national standards covering AI fairness, robustness, and incident reporting, while establishing a National Working Group on AI Standardization to align with ITU-T global benchmarks.

The workshop introduced the AI for Good Lab framework, designed to help countries overcome challenges related to limited skills, fragmented innovation, and missing infrastructure through three interconnected pillars. First, the AI Readiness and Policy pillar assesses policy gaps and establishes practical governance frameworks. Second, the AI Skills Development pillar focuses on scaling national AI talent, capacity-building, and training initiatives. Third, the Public AI Infrastructure pillar establishes standards-based, interoperable AI Sandbox environments for testing, validating, scaling, and re-using locally relevant AI solutions. As one of the ten pilot countries alongside partners from Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Gulf, India brings its model of shared compute, open datasets, and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to lead cross-regional learning and technical collaboration across the Global South.

The sessions delivered structured deliberation on defining a concrete roadmap for institutional engagement, priority sector adoption, and Global South knowledge-sharing. Stakeholders achieved a shared understanding of the AI Sandbox requirements to support experimentation while validating fairness, robustness, and safety before scaling solutions to the last citizen.

The workshop concluded with a summary by Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, followed by a Call for Follow-up Actions by Shri Sanjeev Kumar Sharma, Deputy Director General, AI & Digital Intelligence Unit, DoT, and special address by Shri S. T. Abbas, Sr. Deputy Director General, TEC.

The workshop reinforced the importance of sustained collaboration among Government, industry, academia, startups, civil society and international organisations to build an AI ecosystem that is innovative, inclusive, secure, trusted and beneficial for all. The discussions provided a strong foundation for moving from dialogue to implementation, from vision to action and from isolated initiatives to a collaborative movement for AI for Good and AI for All.

Union Ayush Minister inaugurates Indo-UK Health Conclave 2026; welcomes structured training programme for Ayush professionals
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, today emphasised that traditional systems of medicine, when supported by scientific research, appropriate clinical evidence, quality standards and responsible integration, can make a significant contribution to strengthening preventive healthcare and holistic well-being across the world.

The Minister inaugurated the second edition of Indo-UK Health Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, organised by Marengo Asia Hospitals and BAPIO Training Academy, held under the theme “Bridging Healthcare, Education and Innovation”. The two-day event brings together healthcare professionals, academicians and institutional representatives from India and the United Kingdom.

Welcoming the launch of a structured training and capacity-building initiative for Ayush professionals, Shri Jadhav said that scientific research, appropriate clinical evidence, quality standards and responsible integration can enable traditional systems of medicine to contribute significantly to preventive healthcare and holistic well-being.

The initiative includes two six-month certificate courses for Ayush graduates and postgraduates: Certificate in Acute Care & Emergency Support and Certificate in Lifestyle Health & Well-Being Counselling & Practice. The programmes aim to strengthen clinical-support skills and preventive health counselling through structured teaching and supervised practical training.

Highlighting the complementary strengths of both countries, the Minister noted that the UK's experience in clinical governance, patient safety and quality assurance, combined with India's clinical expertise, technological innovation and healthcare delivery capabilities, can help build more effective and accountable healthcare systems.

Shri Jadhav congratulated the organisers and participating institutions, expressing confidence that the conclave would translate discussions into sustained partnerships and concrete outcomes for both countries' healthcare systems.

The conclave is expected to further deepen institutional cooperation between India and the United Kingdom, while creating new opportunities for knowledge exchange, professional development and innovation in healthcare delivery.

2321457.title: “Immense Opportunities in Food Processing; Youth Should Become Job Creators, Not Job Seekers”: Shri Chirag Paswan
2321457.body_html:
Ministry of Food Processing Industries
“Immense Opportunities in Food Processing; Youth Should Become Job Creators, Not Job Seekers”: Shri Chirag Paswan
260 students receive degrees at NIFTEM-K’s 7th Convocation; 8 meritorious students awarded Gold Medals 
Quality of Indian products is closely linked to the global reputation of ‘Brand India’: Shri Chirag Paswan
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Food Processing Industries, Shri Chirag Paswan, today said that India’s food processing sector offers immense opportunities and has the potential to play a major role in generating employment, promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening farmers’ incomes and enhancing India’s global presence. Shri Paswan is the Union Minister for Food Processing Industries, while Shri Avinash Joshi is the Secretary of the Ministry.

Addressing the 7th Convocation of the National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management, Kundli (NIFTEM-K), Shri Paswan urged graduating students not to restrict themselves to becoming job seekers, but to emerge as job creators, innovators and solution providers. NIFTEM-K’s official portal also identifies the 2026 event as its 7th Convocation.

He said that despite the progress made in recent years, the food processing sector continues to offer enormous untapped potential. The sector can contribute simultaneously to better food quality, value addition, stronger economic opportunities for farmers, employment generation and reduction of food wastage.

Shri Paswan said India’s vast agricultural base, diversity of produce and large consumer market give the country the strength to emerge as a “Global Food Basket”. He underlined the need to take food value chains, processing facilities and technology closer to farms and rural areas so that the benefits of food processing reach producers at the grassroots.

Calling upon students to think beyond conventional pathways, he urged them to use technology, innovation and entrepreneurship to find solutions to emerging challenges. He assured young innovators that the Government would support new ideas and initiatives aimed at strengthening the sector.

The Minister also made a strong appeal for maintaining quality, stressing that there should be no compromise on quality in the food sector. He said that the quality of an Indian product affects not merely the reputation of an individual company, but also the standing of “Brand India” in global markets.

Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Shri Avinash Joshi, highlighted the wider role of food processing in reducing food wastage, enhancing nutrition and value addition, creating livelihood opportunities and encouraging entrepreneurship. He emphasised the importance of developing skilled human resources and encouraging students and researchers to pursue ideas and innovations that can create value on a larger scale.

Dr. Trilochan Mohapatra, Chairman, Board of Governors, NIFTEM-K, emphasised that the knowledge and skills acquired by students should contribute not only to their individual careers but also to the progress of the country and society. NIFTEM-K officially lists Dr. Mohapatra as Chairperson of its Board of Governors.

He stressed the need to strengthen NIFTEM-K’s research, skilled human resource and innovation ecosystem, and called for disruptive innovations that could help India achieve global leadership in food technology, safe and nutritious food, sustainable processing and value addition. Joshi Sir Sec

NIFTEM-K Director Dr. Harinder Singh Oberoi said that the Institute has made significant progress in academics, research, infrastructure and industry partnerships.

A total of 260 students received degrees at the Convocation, comprising 140 B.Tech., 78 M.Tech., 18 MBA and 24 Ph.D. students. Eight meritorious students were awarded Gold Medals in recognition of their academic excellence and dedication.

Dr. Oberoi said that NIFTEM-K’s endeavour is to equip students not only with academic qualifications but also with capabilities in research, innovation, entrepreneurship and industry-oriented learning, enabling them to respond effectively to the evolving needs of the food sector.

Dr. R. S. Sodhi, President (Food and Agriculture), Reliance Retail Ltd., said that this was one of the most opportune times for professionals to enter India’s food sector. His current industry designation is President (Food and Agriculture), Reliance Retail Ltd.

Dr. Sodhi described food as a relatively recession-resilient sector, noting that while consumers may postpone several discretionary purchases, food remains an essential everyday requirement. He said that with a population of more than 1.4 billion and changing consumption patterns, India offers substantial opportunities across the food value-addition ecosystem.

Shri Deepak Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Bikaji Foods International Limited, encouraged graduating students to make full use of emerging opportunities in the food industry and described them as the future of the sector. Bikaji’s official corporate information confirms Shri Agarwal as Chairman and Managing Director.

The speakers collectively underlined that NIFTEM-K’s role extends beyond academic education. As an institution connecting research, industry, entrepreneurship and Government, it has the potential to play an increasingly important role in strengthening India’s food processing ecosystem and nurturing the next generation of innovators, professionals and entrepreneurs.

2321441.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Kathgodam to Dehradun Railway under UPW LSA, during the month of August 2026
2321441.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Kathgodam to Dehradun Railway under UPW LSA, during the month of August 2026
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Kathgodam to Dehradun Railway route passing through Haldwani, Lal Kuan, Rudrapur City, Rampur, Moradabad, Najibabad Junction, Haridwar etc.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted through its appointed agency across Kathgodam to Dehradun Railway under UPW LSA, during the month of August 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). The performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, captured during IDT are published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. `

These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Bhopal. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

The drive tests conducted across City drive – 335.8 KMs Kathgodam to Dehradun Railway  from 13th August 2026 in UP West LSA.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

 

 Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence (Mute) Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence (Mute) Instance: Number of call silence (Mute) instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

The overall mobile network performance in Kathgodam to Dehradun railway route for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, were 2833/ 23986 for Airtel, 6638/ 23597 for BSNL, 1734/ 23643 for RJIL and 2774/ 24080 for VIL for Kathgodam to Dehradun railway route. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 5/ 115 for Airtel, 24/ 129 for BSNL, 5/ 124 for RJIL and 6/ 126 for VIL for Kathgodam to Dehradun railway route. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 113.02 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 10.84 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 156.76 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 36.32 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Kathgodam to Dehradun railway route. Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 16.60 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 4.83 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 18.18 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 8.47 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Kathgodam to Dehradun railway route. Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: -

  1. Railway Route - Kathgodam to Dehradun passing through Haldwani, Lal Kuan, Rudrapur City, Rampur, Moradabad, Najibabad Junction, Haridwar etc.

2321422.title: The Indian Parliamentary Delegation led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, continued its participation in the 153rd IPU Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on the fourth day of the Assembly, i.e. 08 October 2026
2321422.body_html:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
The Indian Parliamentary Delegation led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, continued its participation in the 153rd IPU Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on the fourth day of the Assembly, i.e. 08 October 2026
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, and Members of the Delegation attended the debate on the emergency item, “Urgent parliamentary action to address climate-related disasters and strengthen resilience in the Himalayan region and other vulnerable regions”, which was proposed by Nepal and adopted on the third day of the 153rd Assembly of the IPU. The Indian Delegation also attended the continuation of the General Debate on the theme “Enhancing good governance and empowering communities through inclusivity, trust and opportunities for all”.

Dr. Anurag Singh Thakur, MP, Lok Sabha, participated in the debate on the aforesaid emergency item and spoke in its support, placing on record India’s point of view. He thereafter participated in the meeting of the Bureau of the Standing Committee on Democracy and Human Rights and conveyed the position of the Indian Parliament on the future subject items to be considered by the Committee for presentation of a resolution to a future Assembly. He also attended the meeting of the said Standing Committee and contributed to the adoption of the Resolution.

Dr. Sasmit Patra, MP, Rajya Sabha, attended the meeting of the Standing Committee on United Nations Affairs and participated in the panel discussion on “The UN machinery for conflict prevention and resolution: How does it work?”. He also attended the hearing with the candidates for the position of IPU President, ahead of the election scheduled for 09 October 2026, the last day of the 153rd IPU Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania.

Dr. Lata Wankhede, MP, Lok Sabha, attended the meeting of the Standing Committee on Sustainable Development and participated in the panel discussion on “Artificial intelligence and the future of work”.

The Secretary-General, Rajya Sabha, attended the meeting of the Association of Secretaries General of Parliaments (ASGP) and participated in the informal discussion group connected with the General Debate on “How is Parliament funded, and what are the processes for allocating and approving the budget?”. The Secretary-General apprised the participants of the budgetary processes of the Indian Parliament.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives of Australia, Mr. Milton Dick was declared elected today, the 9th October 2026, as the President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union at the 153rd IPU Assembly held in Arusha, United Republic of Tanzania. Immediately after the announcement of the result, Shri Harivansh Hon'ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha and other Members of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation to Arusha, personally congratulated him and wished for a successful tenure as the President of the IPU.
