2319589.title: DRDO Conducts Maiden Live Jump of Advanced High-Altitude Parachute
2319589.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
DRDO Conducts Maiden Live Jump of Advanced High-Altitude Parachute
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden live jump of the Advanced High-Altitude Parachute (AHAP) at one of the highest-altitude drop zones, Nyoma (Mudh DZ).

The jump was executed at 16,000 feet above mean sea level (AMSL). The parachute was deployed at 15500 feet AMSL and landing was undertaken at Nyoma (Mudh DZ) which is at 13,700 feet. The jump proved the efficacy and tactical employability of the AHAP parachute at extremely High-Altitude Terrains.

Designed and developed by Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra, AHAP is a static line parachute system for mass drop of paratroopers.

The system has been manufactured by Ordnance Parachute Factory (OPF) Kanpur, inspected by DGAQA and certified by CEMILAC, RCMA Kanpur.

AHAP offers various deployment modes, has a very wide operational altitude range (up to 18000 ft) and has the safest rate of descent especially suited for the tactical requirements of the Indian Defence Forces for high-altitude terrains. Static line parachute jumps at these high altitudes are complex and inherently risky owing to very high opening shock and rate of descent.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh complimented DRDO, Defence Forces, DPSUs and Industry on the successful maiden live jump of AHAP indigenous parachute system and termed it as another big step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D & Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh congratulated the team members associated with the design and development of the system.

2319567.title: “Yuva Shakti is the Strength of Viksit Bharat”: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
2319567.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2319567.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
“Yuva Shakti is the Strength of Viksit Bharat”: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
MY Bharat’s Points, Rewards and Recognition Mechanism to Turn Youth Participation into Recognition, Opportunity and Leadership
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), is operationalising a Points, Rewards and Recognition (PRR) Mechanism on the MY Bharat Portal to recognise and encourage sustained participation of young people in volunteering, experiential learning, youth development initiatives and other nation-building activities.

Highlighting the importance of youth participation in the nation-building process, Union Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said, “Yuva Shakti is the strength of Viksit Bharat. Through MY Bharat’s PRR mechanism, the Modi Government is turning youth participation into recognition, opportunity and leadership.”

The PRR mechanism introduces a structured, milestone-based system through which youth will receive recognition, rewards and opportunities based on the points accumulated through their engagement on the MY Bharat Portal. The initiative seeks to motivate young people to sustain their participation in volunteering, experiential learning, civic engagement and youth development activities, while encouraging them to strive towards higher milestones.

Under the mechanism, youth achieving 1,000 points will receive a formal MY Bharat Letter of Recognition, signed by the Director, MY Bharat Division. At the 2,500-point milestone, eligible participants will be recognised through the official MY Bharat social media handles, subject to a consent-based mechanism for publication of their name, photograph and MY Bharat ID.

Youth attaining 5,000 points will be featured in a dedicated MY Bharat Digital Hall of Fame on the MY Bharat Portal. The Hall of Fame will showcase the achiever’s name, MY Bharat ID, photograph and a brief profile drawn from the public profile. A facility for other users to send messages to achievers may also be explored, subject to appropriate safeguards.

The mechanism provides progressively enhanced rewards at higher milestones. Youth achieving 7,500 points will receive the hardbound book Modi@20. Those reaching 10,000 points will be eligible to receive a signed hardbound copy of The Golden Road: How Ancient India Transformed the World by William Dalrymple, signed by the Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports. At the 20,000-point milestone, eligible achievers will receive a signed hardbound copy of Treasures of India: From Antiquity to Modernity by DK, signed by the Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports.

The higher milestones under the PRR mechanism are designed to provide young achievers with opportunities for direct interaction with senior leadership. At the 50,000-point milestone, eligible youth will have an opportunity to meet the Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports during an upcoming edition of the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) or another suitable major youth engagement event. The eligible achievers will be identified from the Portal and their details verified by MY Bharat Headquarters.

At the highest proposed milestone of 1,00,000 points, eligible youth will have an opportunity to meet the Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports during an upcoming edition of VBYLD. The selected youth will be identified through the MY Bharat Portal and their details verified by MY Bharat Headquarters. The felicitation of youth achieving the 50,000 and 1,00,000-point milestones is proposed to commence from October 2027.

The PRR mechanism establishes a progressive pathway that begins with formal recognition and digital visibility and extends to tangible rewards and opportunities to engage with national youth leadership platforms. Through the initiative, MY Bharat seeks to create a sustained culture of participation, service and leadership among India’s youth.

The initiative reinforces the vision of “Samarth Yuva, Viksit Bharat”, recognising that active and empowered youth are central to India’s journey towards a developed nation. By acknowledging individual contributions and creating opportunities for further engagement, the PRR mechanism seeks to inspire young citizens to continue their journey of leadership, community service and nation-building through MY Bharat.

2319565.title: Cabinet passes  resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 25 Years of Unbroken Leadership
2319565.body_html:
Cabinet
Cabinet passes resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 25 Years of Unbroken Leadership
10 Defining Highlights of the Union Cabinet Resolution
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet today passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of Nation First and Citizen First. Three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM Narendra Modi

These ten salient features capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India.

  1. From Gujarat to India A Development Vision Grows

The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India.

  1. Compassion for the Poor Becomes Dignity at Scale

PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity.

  1. Empowerment Opens Doors Across Society

PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became LakhpatiDidis, while the Nari Shakti VandanAdhiniyam provided for women’s reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded ₹4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind.

  1. An Unwavering Commitment to Reform

The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. His appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose.

  1. Building the Foundations of a Self-Reliant India

Under PM Modi’s leadership, Public capital expenditure rose from ₹2 lakh crore to over ₹12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around ₹2 lakh crore to more than ₹13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs.

  1. Technology Serves Citizens and Expands National Ambition

PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. Developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities.

7. Steadfast Leadership Through Turbulent Times

The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval. During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. His leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times.

8. Decisive Leadership Secures Peace and Confidence

2016 Surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot Air Strikes and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff’s post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust.

9. India’s Voice Grows Stronger on the World Stage

The resolution links India’s rising stature with PM Modi’s ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union’s G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how India’s capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and India’s growing influence and contribution to shared solutions.

10. Progress Draws Strength from Heritage and Responsibility

PM Modi’s vision unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarat’s dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lalla’s consecration strengthened India’s connection with its heritage. The resolution culminates in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047.

2319563.title: India, Switzerland Strengthen Strategic Science & Technology Partnership; Dr. Jitendra Singh Holds Bilateral Meeting with Swiss President Guy Parmelin
2319563.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India, Switzerland Strengthen Strategic Science & Technology Partnership; Dr. Jitendra Singh Holds Bilateral Meeting with Swiss President Guy Parmelin
Dr. Jitendra Singh and Swiss President Guy Parmelin discuss expanding long-term cooperation in science, research and innovation
India’s mission-mode approach in AI, quantum, biotechnology, space and deep ocean research opens new avenues for bilateral collaboration, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Indo-Swiss Research Framework, Joint Scientific Board and new institutional agreements to further strengthen research ecosystem
Switzerland earmarks CHF 45 million for further strengthening the Indo-Swiss research partnership
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today held a bilateral meeting with President of the Swiss Confederation, H.E. Guy Parmelin, in New Delhi, with discussions focused on further strengthening the longstanding India-Switzerland partnership in science, technology, research and innovation. The meeting focused on taking the bilateral S&T partnership into a more structured and long-term phase, with greater institutional engagement and cooperation in emerging areas of mutual interest.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is increasingly adopting an interdisciplinary and mission-mode approach to Science and Technology, with national programmes bringing together expertise from different disciplines and ministries. He said Artificial Intelligence is being viewed as an enabling tool rather than a separate discipline, with the potential to contribute across diverse areas of science and technology.

Referring to India’s expanding S&T priorities, he spoke about the country’s work in biotechnology, vaccine development, genome sequencing, quantum technology, space and deep ocean research, as well as the emerging opportunities in the blue economy and bio-economy.

Dr. Jitendra Singh welcomed the progress towards the Indo-Swiss Research Framework (ISRF) and the Indo-Swiss Joint Scientific Board, which provide a stronger basis for taking bilateral S&T cooperation towards a strategic and long-term framework. He also welcomed the Letter of Intent between the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and the Department of Science & Technology (DST) and the Implementation Agreement between the Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW) and DST, and said these initiatives would further strengthen institutional engagement and research collaboration between the two countries.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the cordial relationship between India and Switzerland makes it easier for the two countries to collaborate at different levels and stressed the need for a regular working arrangement to ensure sustained engagement and effective follow-up on areas of mutual interest. He said the two sides could continue working together to deepen cooperation in research, innovation and emerging technologies.

President Guy Parmelin said Switzerland sees India as a rapidly emerging global research and development power and seeks to position itself as a preferred long-term partner in education, research and innovation. Recalling the bilateral Science and Technology Agreement signed in 2003, he said the partnership has grown steadily and that Switzerland is committed to developing a more structured and long-term framework for cooperation.

President Parmelin said Switzerland has earmarked a further CHF 45 million for the partnership, and expressed the expectation of a corresponding commitment from India to further strengthen and consolidate the joint Indo-Swiss research framework. He expressed confidence that the two countries can achieve much more by building on their longstanding scientific partnership and working closely together.

The two sides also discussed Artificial Intelligence and its wider applications, with President Parmelin stressing the importance of ensuring that AI benefits countries across the Global South. He also invited Indian participation in the forthcoming Geneva AI Summit, reflecting the shared interest in expanding cooperation in emerging technologies and areas of global significance.

India and Switzerland have built more than two decades of cooperation in Science and Technology since the signing of the Inter-Governmental Agreement in 2003. The partnership has evolved through the Indo-Swiss Joint Research Programme and has expanded into areas including quantum technology, Artificial Intelligence, clean technology, renewable energy, ocean research and blue economy, advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, biomedical research, pandemic preparedness and space technologies.

The Indo-Swiss Research Framework now seeks to take this cooperation from a project-based model towards a more strategic, system-level partnership, with enhanced mobility, knowledge exchange and long-term cooperation.

The meeting was attended from the Swiss side by Dr. Martina Hirayama, State Secretary for Education, Research & Innovation (SERI); H.E. Maya Tissafi, Ambassador of Switzerland to India and Bhutan; Catherine von Wyl, Scientific Advisor, SERI; Prof. Dr. Torsten Schwede, President, Swiss National Science Foundation; Thomas Gfeller, Chief Executive Officer, Foundation Switzerland Innovation; Prof. Dr. Regula Jöhl, President, Zurich University of Applied Sciences; Joël François Mesot, President, ETH Zurich; and Leena Arora Kukreja, Science & Technology Counsellor, Embassy of Switzerland.

From the Indian side, Dr. Jitendra Singh was accompanied by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology; Dr. Rajesh Sudhir Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology; Dr. Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Head, ICD, DST; and Dr. Ramkrishna Sahoo, Nodal, Swiss Desk, DST, during the meeting.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India and Switzerland, building on their cordial and longstanding relationship, can establish a regular working arrangement to sustain engagement and ensure continued follow-up on bilateral Science and Technology initiatives. He expressed confidence that the two countries can further deepen their partnership by working together across emerging areas of science, technology and innovation.

2319560.title: Indo-Swiss Research Framework to Give Fresh Impetus to Two Decades of Scientific Cooperation and Open New Avenues for Joint Research and Innovation: Dr. Jitendra Singh
2319560.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Indo-Swiss Research Framework to Give Fresh Impetus to Two Decades of Scientific Cooperation and Open New Avenues for Joint Research and Innovation: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Flagship Event celebrates two decades of India-Switzerland partnership and charts roadmap for deeper, structured and long-term collaboration
New framework to strengthen research networks, mobility, knowledge exchange and academia-industry linkages, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Explore and Academia-Industry Training programmes to create new opportunities for researchers, innovators and startups
DST-SNSF Letter of Intent and DST-ZHAW Implementation Arrangement mark new phase of bilateral S&T partnership
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today said that the Indo-Swiss Research Framework (ISRF) will give fresh impetus to the longstanding India-Switzerland Science, Technology and Innovation partnership and provide a structured platform for taking bilateral cooperation into new and emerging areas.

Addressing the inaugural Indo-Swiss Research Flagship Event 2026 in New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the event was an occasion not only to celebrate two decades of healthy and progressively expanding cooperation, but also to chart the way forward by diversifying the partnership into emerging areas of Science, Technology and Innovation and creating greater opportunities for researchers and innovators in both countries.

The Flagship Event, held at New Delhi, brought together H.E. Guy Parmelin, President of the Swiss Confederation; H.E. Maya Tissafi, Ambassador of Switzerland to India and Bhutan; Dr. Martina Hirayama, State Secretary for Education, Research & Innovation; Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology, and senior representatives of research institutions, funding agencies, universities and the wider innovation ecosystem.

The programme was structured around two broad themes, “Looking back on 20 Years of Impact and Excellence” and “Looking forward: Transforming Tomorrow Together”, reflecting both the achievements of the partnership and its future direction.

Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled that the formal foundation of India-Switzerland cooperation in Science and Technology was laid with the signing of the Inter-Governmental Agreement in 2003, followed by mechanisms for periodic review and expansion of the partnership. The Indo-Swiss Joint Research Programme, initiated in 2005, has since provided a platform for bringing together faculty and young researchers from both countries in areas of strategic relevance.

The Indo-Swiss Joint Committee on Science & Technology has also played an important role in reviewing ongoing cooperation and shaping future engagements, with seven rounds held so far, the latest in Bern in September 2025.

The Minister said the partnership has steadily expanded through the participation of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), in collaboration with Swiss institutions, particularly the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). This broad-based cooperation today spans research areas including mountain and glacier studies, geoscientific hazards, systems medicine, One Health and social sciences.

The expanding breadth of the partnership was also reflected in the event presentation, which showcased successive Indo-Swiss research initiatives across biomedical research, renewable energy, life sciences, systems medicine, social sciences and mountain research, with the 2026 initiatives further advancing cooperation in mountain hazards, social sciences and One Health. This progression reflects the growing thematic and institutional depth of India-Switzerland research cooperation.

Dr. Jitendra Singh spoke about strong collaboration between MoES and SNSF in mountain and glacier research and geoscientific hazards in mountain regions. The cooperation has already supported four Indo-Swiss projects covering glacier evolution, ice nucleating particles, water vapour isotopes and debris-glacier interactions, with the partnership subsequently expanded towards geoscientific hazards.

He also referred to the growing engagement in One Health between SNSF, DBT and ICMR, as well as cooperation between ICSSR and SNSF in areas such as digital governance, AI ethics and the social impact of Artificial Intelligence, inequality, justice and inclusion, mobility and social integration, and economic transformation.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Indo-Swiss Research Framework represents a new and more strategic phase in the relationship, moving the partnership towards a structured, system-level approach to long-term cooperation. The framework is designed to strengthen mobility, knowledge exchange, research networking and sustained collaboration, while opening new avenues for cooperation aligned with national priorities and globally relevant areas of Science, Technology and Innovation.

As part of this forward-looking agenda, the Minister welcomed new initiatives including “Explore”, aimed at building new research networks with the vision of developing larger consortia, and the Academia-Industry Training (AIT) programme for science-based innovators. The event presentation also showcased the forthcoming Explore programme, scheduled to open in November 2026 as a co-funded SNSF-DST initiative, with a 9–12-month duration and support for travel, networking and small equipment to help new ideas in basic science develop into larger research opportunities.

The Minister also welcomed the Letter of Intent between DST and SNSF and the Implementation Arrangement between DST and Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW). The LoI will support exploratory scientific collaboration, future joint research and long-term cooperation across mutually agreed priority areas, while the Implementation Arrangement will advance cooperation in innovation, technology transfer and entrepreneurship through the Indo-Swiss Academia-Industry Training (AIT India) programme.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the new funding and cooperation mechanisms under the Indo-Swiss Research Framework will complement the existing research, technology and innovation ecosystems of both countries and open new horizons for researchers. He expressed confidence that the renewed momentum in bilateral cooperation would enable India and Switzerland to move at an even faster pace in the coming years, with the next phase of the partnership becoming more expansive, impactful and mutually rewarding.

President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin said India and Switzerland share important values, including a strong commitment to excellence, a belief in the power of knowledge and a conviction that science and innovation can contribute to addressing the needs of society. He said the foundations of the bilateral research partnership are strong and welcomed the new Indo-Swiss Research Framework as a new chapter in cooperation. President Parmelin said India’s rapidly growing research and innovation ecosystem and Switzerland’s internationally recognised research excellence, competitive funding mechanisms and highly connected innovation ecosystem offer significant scope for deeper collaboration.

President Parmelin also welcomed the framework’s focus on connecting researchers and institutions, strengthening mobility, exchanging knowledge and skills and creating opportunities for ideas to develop through sustained cooperation. He expressed confidence that the next chapter of Indo-Swiss research cooperation would bring greater ambition, stronger connections and lasting impact.

Ambassador of Switzerland to India and Bhutan Maya Tissafi said that research and innovation have created concrete value in the India-Switzerland relationship, with Switzerland bringing a strong research and innovation ecosystem and India contributing exceptional scientific talent, scale and a rapidly expanding research and technology ecosystem.

She welcomed the opportunity to connect more researchers and translate scientific partnerships into innovation and solutions with real-world impact, while appreciating the importance attached by both countries to strengthening this partnership.

The Flagship Event also showcased the impact of existing cooperation through research presentations spanning mental health and brain research, language and linguistic studies, and Himalayan glacier research, before moving into the forward-looking session on the Indo-Swiss Research Framework and upcoming initiatives.

The programme brought together researchers from current consortia, policymakers and other stakeholders to promote cross-project collaboration, knowledge exchange, policy dialogue and research translation.

The Flagship Event marked an important milestone in the evolution of India-Switzerland Science, Technology and Innovation cooperation, bringing together the achievements of two decades with a clear roadmap for the future. With the Indo-Swiss Research Framework and new initiatives focused on research networks, mobility, knowledge exchange and academia-industry engagement, the two countries are set to deepen a partnership built on scientific excellence, innovation and shared opportunities.

2319427.title: E-Sanjeevani Crosses 50 Crore Teleconsultations, Strengthening Access to Healthcare Across the Country
2319427.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2319427.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
E-Sanjeevani Crosses 50 Crore Teleconsultations, Strengthening Access to Healthcare Across the Country
Women Account for 57.14% of E-Sanjeevani Utilisation; 40.15% Consultations Availed by Citizens Aged 46 Years and Above, Underscoring Wider Reach of Telemedicine
E-Sanjeevani Integrates AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support System and ERSS-112 to Strengthen Digital Healthcare Delivery
E-Sanjeevani Expands Beyond Primary Healthcare, Enables Specialist OPD Consultations Through Premier Government Institutions
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 9:53AM by PIB Delhi

In a landmark achievement, India’s National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore (500 million) teleconsultations, marking a significant milestone in the Government’s efforts to leverage digital technology to make quality healthcare more accessible, affordable and equitable for citizens across the country.

The platform crossed the landmark on September 15, 2026, recording a cumulative 50,00,92,730 teleconsultations across all 36 States and Union Territories. The achievement reflects the growing role of telemedicine in complementing the country’s existing healthcare delivery system and in overcoming barriers of distance, geography and access, particularly for citizens living in rural, remote and underserved areas.

As the world’s largest telemedicine implementation in primary healthcare, eSanjeevani has emerged as an important component of India’s digital health ecosystem. By enabling citizens to consult healthcare professionals remotely, the platform has extended the reach of public healthcare services beyond the physical boundaries of conventional health facilities and brought medical consultations closer to people in the communities where they live.

The service has witnessed rapid and sustained expansion since its inception. eSanjeevani currently supports more than 1.42 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes, 19,473 medical hubs and 901 online OPDs, with 2,41,923 registered healthcare providers. Available in 15 languages, including English and 14 Indian languages, the platform is facilitating approximately 2.5–3 lakh consultations every day. Its highest single-day utilisation has reached 6,30,315 consultations, reflecting the increasing acceptance and utilisation of telemedicine services across the country.

The utilisation pattern of eSanjeevani also highlights its growing relevance among population groups for whom access to physical healthcare facilities may involve greater travel, time or logistical challenges. Women account for 57.14 per cent of total utilisation, while 40.15 per cent of consultations are availed by citizens aged 46 years and above, including 16.25 per cent by senior citizens aged 60 years and above. The significant participation of women and older citizens underscores the potential of telemedicine to make healthcare more convenient and accessible while complementing services available through the public health system.

The platform has continued to evolve with the integration of emerging technologies aimed at strengthening the quality of telemedicine services. A key recent advancement is the integration of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Clinical Decision Support System (AI-CDSS), which supports healthcare providers during consultations and assists in strengthening the quality, consistency and efficiency of clinical decision-making. The innovation has received national recognition with the Gold Award under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026.

In another significant step towards strengthening integrated healthcare delivery, eSanjeevani has also been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS)-112, enabling stronger linkages between emergency response services and remote medical expertise. The integration is aimed at facilitating more coordinated access to medical support and further strengthening the use of digital technology in emergency healthcare.

Building on its extensive primary healthcare network, eSanjeevani is now expanding beyond primary healthcare to facilitate specialist OPD consultations through premier government medical institutions. Patient-to-doctor teleconsultation services for select specialities have been rolled out at AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Jammu and AIIMS Patna, enabling patients to access specialist consultations remotely from their homes.

The initiative is expected to reduce the need for patients to undertake long-distance travel and wait for consultations at tertiary-care facilities, while improving access to specialist medical expertise. The facility is envisaged for progressive expansion to other premier government institutions, including AIIMS, JIPMER and PGIMER Chandigarh, thereby complementing conventional in-person OPD services and strengthening the continuum of care.

The expansion of specialist teleconsultation services marks an important evolution in the journey of eSanjeevani. From facilitating consultations at the primary healthcare level, the platform is increasingly enabling linkages across different levels of care, helping connect patients with appropriate medical expertise while making more effective use of the specialist capacity available within the public healthcare system.

eSanjeevani is a Made-in-India digital health solution developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), with C-DAC Mohali providing end-to-end technological development and engineering support since its inception. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has played a central role in guiding the continuous evolution of the platform in response to the emerging needs of India’s healthcare system.

Through sustained collaboration between the Ministry and technology partners, coupled with continuous innovation, eSanjeevani has evolved from its initial hub-and-spoke telemedicine model into a population-scale national digital health platform serving 50 crore consultations. The development and scaling of the platform reflects India’s growing capability to design and deploy indigenous digital public infrastructure for large-scale public healthcare delivery and is aligned with the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

The achievement of 50 crore teleconsultations marks a significant milestone in India’s digital health journey and reflects the growing role of technology in strengthening the country’s public healthcare system. With its expanding reach across primary and specialist care, integration of Artificial Intelligence and emergency response services, and continued expansion to premier tertiary-care institutions, eSanjeevani is emerging as an important enabler of accessible and equitable healthcare.

The continued evolution of the platform underscores the Government’s commitment to harnessing digital public infrastructure and indigenous technological capabilities to bridge geographical barriers, strengthen the continuum of care and advance the goal of Universal Health Coverage, ensuring that quality healthcare is brought closer to citizens across the country.

2319426.title: Ministry of Rural Development Notifies 375 Permissible Works under VB–G RAM G
2319426.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Rural Development Notifies 375 Permissible Works under VB–G RAM G
The new Schedule expands the scope of permissible works by 41 percent compared with the previous scheme
128 works under Water Security, 111 under Core Rural Infrastructure, 98 under Livelihood-related Infrastructure and 38 under Disaster Preparedness
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:29AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development has notified the Schedule of Permissible Works under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) [VB–G RAM G] Act, 2025, providing for 375 permissible works under the new rural works framework.

The new Schedule represents a 41 percent expansion over the 266 works under the previous framework. The works have been reorganised around four thematic pillars — Water Security, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works for Extreme Weather Events and Disaster Preparedness.

The new framework seeks to move beyond a conventional list of asset types and align wage employment with the creation of durable rural assets and measurable development outcomes. Every work will originate through a bottom-up, decentralized planning process under the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan, approved by the Gram Sabha, and will be tracked through the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack.

Water Security gets highest share with 128 works

The Water Security pillar comprises 128 works, the highest among the four categories. It includes check dams, gully plugs, underground dykes, recharge shafts, injection wells, rejuvenation of rivers, rivulets and nallahs, reclamation of waterlogged land and renovation of field water-distribution channels.

The Schedule also provides for drip irrigation, sprinkler systems, rooftop rainwater harvesting and tankas, along with newer interventions such as ice-stupas and artificial glaciers for water conservation and irrigation.

111 works for Core Rural Infrastructure

The Core Rural Infrastructure pillar comprises 111 works aimed at strengthening essential civic and community infrastructure in rural areas.

These include solar street lighting, waste-to-wealth recycling plants, greywater treatment units, segregation sheds, rural libraries, veterinary and rural health centres, Common Service Centres, multipurpose youth centres, community facilities and additional classrooms and laboratories in government schools.

The framework also provides for repair and maintenance of Jal Jeevan Mission water-supply infrastructure, along with rural parks, footpaths and other village-level amenities.

98 works to strengthen rural livelihoods and value chains

The new framework gives significantly greater emphasis to Livelihood-related Infrastructure, with 98 permissible works.

The category includes agro-processing and value-addition infrastructure, cleaning, grading and packaging units, cold storage facilities, mini flour mills, market yards, dairy infrastructure, mushroom cultivation sheds, sericulture sheds, poly-houses and aquaculture structures.

It also provides infrastructure for Self-Help Groups and their federations, including SHG worksheds, SHE Marts and federation buildings, as well as training-cum-skill development centres. The share of livelihood-related works rises substantially, accounting for 26 per cent of the total permissible works under the new framework, compared with 1.1 per cent under the previous framework.

38 works dedicated to Disaster Preparedness and Climate Resilience

For the first time, a dedicated category for disaster preparedness and extreme weather events has been incorporated into the rural works framework, comprising 38 works.

These include flood relief shelters, retaining walls, embankment strengthening, flood protection works, post-disaster restoration of rural roads and community assets, and forest-fire management measures such as fire lines and fuel-buffer zones.

The category is aimed at strengthening rural communities and assets against floods, cyclones, storms, droughts, landslides, forest fires and other extreme weather events.

Focus on Farmers, Vulnerable Households, Women and Rural Youth

The Schedule places particular emphasis on agriculture, vulnerable households, women and rural youth.

A total of 181 works are agriculture and allied works, including 52 individual-beneficiary works, covering water, land, plantation, livestock and other productive assets that can directly support farmers.

107 works are tagged for Antyodaya/vulnerable households, including 68 individual-beneficiary works. These include housing, sanitation, energy, irrigation, plantations, livestock shelters and other household-level assets.

The framework also includes 36 works related to Nari Shakti and 36 works related to Yuva Shakti, covering infrastructure for women’s collectives, SHGs and federations, youth centres, skill development and enterprise-linked infrastructure.

Inclusive and Future-Ready Rural Infrastructure

The new Schedule provides explicit provisions for Divyangjan accessibility, including construction of stairs and ramps in government buildings. It also includes emergency evacuation and relief shelters in border areas, renewable-energy infrastructure and circular-economy interventions such as waste-to-wealth recycling and greywater treatment.

Works to be planned through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans

Under VB–G RAM G, works will be planned through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans, based on local needs and approved by the Gram Sabha. The digital tracking mechanism through the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack will facilitate convergence of investments across Central, State and local schemes while helping avoid duplication.

The new Schedule thus seeks to align employment generation with water security, durable rural infrastructure, livelihood creation, climate resilience and inclusive development, contributing to the vision of a Viksit Bharat @2047.

2319425.title: Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh Underscores India’s Rising Maritime Power, Indigenous Naval Capability and Strategic Strength at Barakhana in Visakhapatnam
2319425.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh Underscores India’s Rising Maritime Power, Indigenous Naval Capability and Strategic Strength at Barakhana in Visakhapatnam
Highlights Indian Navy’s growing combat prowess and its pivotal role in safeguarding India’s maritime interests
Calls for harnessing India’s vast maritime potential to drive national prosperity, economic growth and strategic power
Pays tribute to Naval Personnel and families for their courage, dedication and contribution to national security
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 10:49PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh attended a Barakhana organised by the Eastern Naval Command in Visakhapatnam on October 05, 2026 and interacted with Indian Navy personnel and their families. He commended the naval personnel for their unwavering commitment to safeguarding the nation’s maritime interests and acknowledged the contribution and sacrifices of their families, whose support enables them to discharge their duties with dedication and commitment.


Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh said the Barakhana provided an opportunity to interact with the naval fraternity and reaffirmed the Government’s appreciation of the dedicated service rendered by the personnel. He conveyed his continued support to the personnel and their families and recognised their commitment and contribution towards national security.

The Raksha Mantri highlighted the Indian Navy’s emergence as a powerful maritime force and its proven ability to respond decisively to challenges confronting the nation. He said the Navy’s capabilities are recognised across the Indo-Pacific and commended its personnel for remaining steadfast in all weather and operational conditions while ensuring the security of India’s maritime boundaries and keeping the Tricolour flying high. Recalling the Navy’s glorious record of valour, he referred to its decisive role during the 1971 War, particularly Operation Trident, when Indian naval forces struck Karachi harbour. He said the operation demonstrated the Navy’s capability not only to safeguard India’s maritime frontiers but also to project power and undertake offensive operations against the adversary when required. He paid tribute to the personnel whose courage and sacrifice continue to inspire generations.

Emphasising India’s transformation as a maritime power, Shri Rajnath Singh said the Indian Navy has kept pace with the changing security environment of the 21st century, with the country developing and inducting advanced and indigenous platforms, including indigenous aircraft carriers, nuclear submarines, stealth frigates and Scorpène-class submarines. He stressed that the strength of the Navy extends beyond ships, submarines and advanced technology and rests fundamentally on the professionalism, patriotism, courage and commitment of its personnel. He said India’s endeavour is to ensure that its waters reflect the nation’s maritime might, its warships embody Indian technology and the Navy’s operations reflect the country’s growing confidence and self-reliance.

Calling for a broader maritime vision, the Raksha Mantri said India must move forward with the philosophy of ‘advancing from the seas towards prosperity and power’, with the oceans viewed not merely as maritime boundaries requiring protection but also as an avenue for economic development, strategic influence and national prosperity.

Describing naval personnel as heroes and an inspiration to the youth, Shri Rajnath Singh said that they represent India’s future, India’s strength and India’s pride. He expressed confidence that their continued dedication and commitment would contribute significantly to India’s emergence as a stronger, more prosperous and self-reliant nation. He also underlined the important role played by the families of Defence Forces personnel, noting that while naval personnel remain deployed at sea in the service of the nation, their families shoulder responsibilities at home and provide the support and strength required for them to discharge their duties effectively. He described the service of the personnel and the sacrifices of their families as a valuable national asset.

Highlighting the informal and familial spirit of the Barakhana, Shri Rajnath Singh said that such occasions provide an opportunity to strengthen the bond between Defence Forces personnel, their families and the leadership. He observed that food is not merely a means of satisfying hunger but also a simple and profound expression of affection and togetherness, as people traditionally invite those with whom they share a special bond to their homes for a meal. He said the Barakhana similarly symbolised the deep relationship between the Defence Forces and the nation, with everyone coming together as part of one larger defence family.

The Raksha Mantri emphasised that the occasion was a reflection of the fraternity, camaraderie and sense of belonging that binds Defence Forces personnel, their families and the leadership. He highlighted the important role of families, noting that while naval personnel remain deployed at sea in the service of the nation, their families shoulder responsibilities at home and provide the strength and support that enable them to discharge their duties effectively. He said that the service of the personnel and the sacrifices of their families together constitute a valuable national asset.

2319423.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA HOSTS PRESIDENT OF THE SWISS CONFEDERATION
2319423.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA HOSTS PRESIDENT OF THE SWISS CONFEDERATION
CLOSE COOPERATION BETWEEN INDIA AND SWITZERLAND CAN BRING IMMENSE BENEFITS TO OUR PEOPLE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 10:40PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu received H.E. Mr Guy Parmelin, President of the Swiss Confederation at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (October 5, 2026). She also hosted a banquet in his honour.

Welcoming President Parmelin to India, the President said that India and Switzerland enjoy warm and cordial relations based on the shared values of democracy and the rule of law. We have extensive cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, culture, and people-to-people contacts. Regular high-level exchanges between our two countries have continued to provide momentum to our bilateral relations.

The President said that Switzerland is an important trade and investment partner for India. She noted that following the implementation of the historic India-European Free Trade Association Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, there are even greater opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment.

The President noted that Swiss companies have invested in India in important sectors and they have a notable presence in India’s infrastructure sector, particularly in the construction of roads, railway bridges and tunnels. She said that they can also explore opportunities in emerging areas such as clean and green technology and Artificial Intelligence.

The President was happy to note that important agreements have been signed during the visit to promote cooperation in migration and mobility, research, and technology transfer.

The two leaders agreed that close cooperation between India and Switzerland can bring immense benefits to the people of both countries. They expressed confidence that this visit will contribute to further strengthening relations between the two countries.

2319421.title: Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Anupriya Patel Launches 14th Edition of India Chem 2026
2319421.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
2319421.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Anupriya Patel Launches 14th Edition of India Chem 2026
Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector Can Become a Key Growth Engine of Indian Economy: Anupriya Patel
India Chem 2026 to be Held in Mumbai from October 22 to 24
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 10:13PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers and Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel, today launched the 14th edition of India Chem 2026, the biennial flagship event of the chemicals and petrochemicals industry. The event will be held in Mumbai from October 22 to 24, 2026.

Addressing the launch event in New Delhi, Smt. Anupriya Patel said that the Government is committed to creating a conducive ecosystem and strengthening infrastructure for the industry to make India self-reliant and realise the vision of a developed India by 2047.

The Minister said that the chemicals and petrochemicals sector has potential to emerge as an important growth engine of the Indian economy. She emphasised the need to align key national initiatives, including the Critical Mineral Mission, Rare Earth Corridor, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, National Manufacturing Mission and FDI reforms, to position India as a global hub for battery chemicals, speciality chemicals and semiconductor chemicals by 2040.

Speaking on the BHAVYA Rasayan Scheme, the Minister said that the scheme should not be viewed as just an infrastructure program but as an attempt to create an environment in which the chemicals and petrochemicals industry can innovate, invest and expand. It was mentioned that the guidelines of the scheme have been released and urged the industry to engage with the state governments for timely submission of the proposals.

The Minister urged industry to increase the spending on R&D along with adopting newer technologies. She further stated that the Department is already pursuing the Department of Science and Technology to declare chemicals and petrochemicals as a priority sector so that it will be covered under the new Research Development Innovation Scheme (RDI) which has an outlay of about 1 lakh Crores. She added that these initiatives would contribute towards achieving the vision of developing the Indian chemical sector into a USD 1 trillion industry by 2040.

Addressing the gathering, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Shri Tejveer Singh, said that the chemicals sector forms the bedrock of India's economic growth and development.

Highlighting the initiatives of the Department, the DCPC Secretary mentioned that the vision of dedicated chemical parks is now close to seeing reality in form of BHAVYA Rasayan scheme. These parks will have best in class facilities including plug and play, proper infrastructure and other facilities so that we are able to bring efficiencies in the cost of production. He also emphasised the need to increase investment in research and development (R&D), stating that sustained investment in R&D is imperative for the growth, innovation and global competitiveness of the sector. He further stated that the Department is working with DPIIT on import substitution exercises in which the chemical and petrochemical sector is included.

Shri Deepankar Aron, Joint Secretary, Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals, Govt. of India while making a presentation on India Chem, mentioned that the aim of the event, which is now in its 14th edition, is to attract investments in the sector along with facilitating B2B partnerships enabling the sector to work together towards growth.

Shri Prabh Das, Chairman, FICCI National Petrochemicals & Plastics Committee and MD & CEO, HPCL-Mittal Energy Ltd., stated that India needs to focus on increased production and there is full support from the Government for the same.

Shri S Ganeshkumar, Co-Chair, FICCI Chemicals Committee and MD, Chemplast Sanmar Ltd said that India’s chemical sector is fully capable to absorb massive capital, leverage FDIs and position itself as the world’s most lucrative chemical industry.

India Chem 2026 is being hosted by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals in partnership with the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI). The 14th edition of the biennial event will comprise an international exhibition and conference, bringing together key stakeholders from the chemicals and petrochemicals sector, including industry leaders, policymakers, investors, researchers and international participants. The event will have sector specific Conclaves on Agrochemicals, Petrochemicals, Speciality Chemicals, as well as on Infrastructure, Environment issues and Process, plant and Machinery. Apart from above, region specific Forums of India-US, India-EU, India-Russia, India-Japan will also take place.

The theme of India Chem 2026 is “Advantage Bharat: An Emerging Global Hub”, reflecting India's growing capabilities and expanding opportunities in the global chemicals and petrochemicals sector.

2319413.title: 2nd Prof. (Dr.) N. R. Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture Held at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre
2319413.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
2nd Prof. (Dr.) N. R. Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture Held at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre
Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant Inaugurates Memorial Lecture
Justice Vikram Nath Delivers Lecture on ‘Judging with Compassion: Human Understanding in the Practice of Law’
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 9:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in collaboration with the Commonwealth Legal Education Association (CLEA), organised the 2nd Prof (Dr.) N. R. Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre in National Capital here, this evening.

The Memorial Lecture, themed ‘Judging with Compassion: Human Understanding in the Practice of Law’, brought together eminent members of the judiciary, legal academia and the legal profession to reflect on the human dimensions of the judicial process and the significance of compassion, empathy and sensitivity in the administration of justice.

The programme was inaugurated by Chief Justice of India, Hon’ble Justice Surya Kant.

Delivering the Memorial Lecture, Hon’ble Justice Vikram Nath, Judge, Supreme Court of India and Executive Chairman, National Legal Services Authority, highlighted the importance of a humane and compassionate approach to the administration of justice, while emphasizing that compassion must remain firmly anchored in the principles of law, fairness and constitutional values.

The programme also featured a special reflection on the life, vision and enduring contribution of Prof. (Dr.) N. R. Madhava Menon by Dr. R. Venkataramani, Learned Attorney General for India.

Prof. (Dr.) S. Sivakumar, Senior Professor, Indian Law Institute, President, CLEA and Member, 21st Law Commission of India, also addressed the gathering.

On the occasion, the Chief Justice of India released two significant publications in the field of law — ‘Indian Personal Law: Unity and Diversity’ and ‘Economics and Law in Context’.

The books have been authored by Prof. (Dr.) S. Sivakumar, with the latter co-authored by Sougata Talukdar. Both publications carry forewords by eminent Judges of the Supreme Court of India.

The books were introduced by Mr. Gowrishankar Natesan, Publisher, Thomson Reuters and Chief Executive Officer, Southshore Innovations Private Limited; Ms. Nabila Zehra, Assistant Professor, School of Law, SGT University, Gurugram; and Dr. Sougata Talukdar, Assistant Professor in Law, Government Centre of Legal Education, University of Burdwan.

The Memorial Lecture commemorates the enduring legacy of Prof. (Dr.) N. R. Madhava Menon, a pioneering legal educator, institution-builder and scholar whose contributions played a transformative role in the development of legal education in India.

The Lecture seeks to carry forward his intellectual legacy by fostering dialogue among the judiciary, legal scholars, practitioners and students on evolving dimensions of law, justice and legal education.

The event witnessed the participation of eminent members of the judiciary, legal fraternity, academia and students.

The programme reaffirmed the importance of compassion, empathy and human understanding as essential dimensions of a responsive and humane justice delivery system, while underscoring the need to uphold the rule of law, constitutional principles and fairness in the administration of justice.

Earlier, in his welcome address, Col. Akash Patil, Director, Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, welcomed the distinguished gathering and underlined the importance of creating platforms for meaningful academic and intellectual engagement on contemporary issues concerning law, justice and society.

Dr. Ruchi Sharma D., Joint General Secretary, CLEA, presented the vote of thanks, bringing the formal proceedings to a close.

2319398.title: MoHUA celebrates World Habitat Day 2026 with focus on advancing affordable, resilient and Inclusive housing
2319398.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
MoHUA celebrates World Habitat Day 2026 with focus on advancing affordable, resilient and Inclusive housing
Best Performing States/UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY 2.0 felicitated at World Habitat Day Celebrations
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) celebrated World Habitat Day 2026 on the theme ‘Adequate Housing for All’ with a focus on strengthening the urban housing ecosystem through innovation, policy reforms, technology and sustainable financing.

The guest of honour for the event was Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs. Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA; Smt. D Thara, Secretary, Department of Capital Development, MoHUA, Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary and Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All/Housing Division, representatives of UN-Habitat, senior officials from Ministry, Principal Secretaries from States and Union Territories and other stakeholders also attended the event, marked by participation of UN agencies, HUDCO, NHB among others.

The celebration provided a platform to highlight India’s continued efforts towards ensuring access to safe, affordable, inclusive and dignified housing, while recognising the contributions of States/UTs and other stakeholders towards achieving the objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) and PMAY-U 2.0.

The event showcased the progress and diverse approaches being adopted towards achieving the objective of “Housing for All”, including best practices under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0. As part of the PMAY-U Awards 2026, Best Performing States/UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 were felicitated, along with ULBs, partner agencies/stakeholders recognising their performance in implementing housing initiatives, including rental housing.

The event also featured videos on best practices related to Housing for All, providing an opportunity to showcase innovative approaches and experiences from across the country for their further replication by other States/UTs.

It was also announced that PMAY-U Awards are being institutionalised to recognise and celebrate exemplary contributions and achievements of States, UTs, ULBs and partner agencies/stakeholders under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban. Furthermore, the awards will be held every year on the occasion of World Habitat Day, highlighting innovative practices, effective implementation and outstanding efforts towards achieving the goal of ‘Housing for All’. This annual recognition will further encourage healthy competition, promote best practices and inspire stakeholders to strengthen the delivery of affordable and quality housing across the country.

The event was also marked by the release of publications of organisations under MoHUA, which included HUDCO, NCHF, NHB, CGEWHO, HUDCO and BMTPC. Apart from the release of publications, prize distribution ceremony for winners of painting competitions organised by NHB, HUDCO and BMTPC for school children, including specially abled children, in various competitions was organised to commemorate the event.

The event also featured the launch of a mobile application and revamped websites of PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, aimed at strengthening access to information and improving the beneficiary experience through digital platforms.

The World Habitat Day event also provided a platform for wider deliberations on emerging urban housing challenges and possible solutions. Three different technical sessions, focussing on rental housing, regulatory frameworks and affordable housing technologies and financing, brought together stakeholders to discuss approaches for expanding access to adequate and affordable housing.

Technical Sessions to Deliberate on Emerging Urban Housing Challenges

It featured thematic technical sessions on topics such as rental housing, bridging the Demand–Supply Gap in housing and role of innovative construction technologies in affordable housing sector, bringing together policymakers, experts, financial institutions, industry stakeholders and other partners to deliberate on key challenges and opportunities for building a stronger and more sustainable housing ecosystem.

The technical deliberations focused on three areas:

1. Structural Challenges and Enabling Measures for Unlocking the Potential of Rental Housing: The session examined the structural and institutional challenges affecting the availability and scalability of rental housing in urban areas. Discussions focused on creating an enabling ecosystem for Affordable Rental Housing, including suitable regulatory frameworks, land and infrastructure availability, investment mechanisms, effective property management and greater participation of public and private sector stakeholders.

The deliberations also explored measures to strengthen rental housing as a viable and dignified housing option for urban migrants, workers, students, working women and other mobile and vulnerable sections of the urban population.

2. Regulatory Measures to Bridge the Demand–Supply Gap in Housing: The second session focused on regulatory and policy measures required to address the persistent mismatch between demand and supply of affordable housing in urban areas. Deliberations covered the need for streamlined approvals, efficient land-use planning, enabling development regulations, improved coordination among stakeholders and measures to facilitate faster delivery of affordable housing.

3. Low-Cost Indigenous Technologies and Financing Instruments for Scaling Resilient and Affordable Housing: The third session focused on the role of innovative, low-cost and indigenous construction technologies in accelerating housing delivery while improving quality, resilience, resource efficiency and affordability.

The discussions emphasised the need to combine technological innovation with appropriate financing solutions to enable large-scale delivery of safe, climate-resilient and affordable homes.

The technical sessions underscored the need for a coordinated approach involving Government, States and UTs, Urban Local Bodies, financial institutions, private sector, technology providers, academia and other stakeholders to address the evolving housing needs of India’s rapidly urbanising population.

The World Habitat Day 2026 celebrations reaffirmed India’s commitment to ensuring that every urban household has access to safe, affordable and dignified housing, contributing to the broader vision of an inclusive and Viksit Bharat.

2319395.title: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Reviews Final Preparations for IMC 2026 at Yashobhoomi
2319395.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Reviews Final Preparations for IMC 2026 at Yashobhoomi
With the theme “Scale Without Boundaries”, IMC 2026 to showcase India’s telecom and digital transformation and growing global technology leadership
Over 1.5 lakh attendees, 500+ exhibitors and partners, 600+ startups and 900+ thought leaders expected
2,000+ technology use cases, 120+ sessions and 700+ investor meetings to drive global collaboration and innovation
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 9:00PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today visited the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 venue at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, to review final preparations ahead of its inauguration Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on October 8th, 2026.

During the visit, the Union Minister took a detailed tour of the exhibition area, interacted with participating startups and exhibitors, and chaired review meetings with senior officials of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), and partner agencies. He also addressed the media, outlining the scale, ambition and global significance of IMC 2026.

Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia stated that “The 10th edition of India Mobile Congress is here. Tremendous amount of excitement, energy, pulsing capabilities and proven model of Indian telecom connectivity. The connectivity on which new frontiers of technology are being explored. Come, be a part of this experience where we will have thousands of exhibitors, hundreds of companies, new products as India moves from a services nation to a product nation..”

With the theme “Scale Without Boundaries”, IMC 2026 will showcase India’s remarkable progress in telecommunications, digital connectivity and technological innovation, while providing a global platform for collaboration, investment and knowledge exchange.

India’s telecom and digital ecosystem has witnessed significant growth in recent years. The country now has 1.01 billion broadband subscribers and over 1 billion internet subscribers, while 5G services cover 99.9 per cent of districts and reach 85 per cent of the population. Further, 98.7 per cent of villages have 4G connectivity, reflecting the rapid expansion of digital connectivity across the country.

India has also emerged as the fifth country in the world to develop its own indigenous 4G stack, marking a significant milestone in the country’s journey towards technological self-reliance and strengthening its capabilities in designing, developing and deploying advanced telecom technologies.

Among the key programmes are the 3rd International 6G Symposium, CTO and CEO Roundtables, discussions on semiconductor and core components supply chains, telecom stacks for the AI era, telecom product manufacturing, satellite communications, 5G monetisation, telecom and quantum convergence, 5G Innovation Hackathon, Startup World Cup, Cybersecurity Summit and initiatives focused on inclusivity, skilling and job creation.

IMC 2026 will feature keynote addresses, roundtables, panel discussions, workshops, hackathons, demonstrations, showcases, bilateral meetings and plenary sessions, providing a platform for collaboration among governments, industry, academia, startups and technology innovators.

The event will also feature the Ministerial Programme on “Investing in the Next Billion Digital Connections”, CEO Roundtable on “The Sovereign Inflection & the Future of Telecom”, AI for Good, Cyber Security Summit, 6G Symposium, Startup World Cup India 2026, ITU Build-A-Thon on AI Agents for 5G Networks, AI Safety India–UK Panel, Robotics for Youth Challenge and other global technology programmes.

The 2026 edition will feature 2,000+ technology use cases and over 120 sessions, providing opportunities for businesses, policymakers, researchers and technology innovators to exchange ideas and explore new partnerships.

The event is also expected to bring together 300+ investors, incubators, accelerators and venture capital firms, with more than 700 investor meetings, creating opportunities for startups and technology enterprises to access global capital, mentorship and markets.

2319373.title: India and Japan Launch Operational Manual for the Joint Crediting Mechanism
2319373.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2319373.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India and Japan Launch Operational Manual for the Joint Crediting Mechanism
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 8:26PM by PIB Delhi

On 30th September, 2026, Ambassador of Japan to India, H.E. Mr. Keiichi Ono and the then Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Tanmay Kumar, jointly launched the Operational Manual for the India–Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM), in New Delhi.

The Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan aims to promote the deployment of advanced low-carbon technologies, mobilize climate finance, facilitate technology cooperation and support high-integrity emission reductions and removals in India. The mechanism will contribute to sustainable development in India while strengthening confidence and transparency in international carbon markets.

The launch of the Manual marks a significant milestone in operationalizing bilateral cooperation between India and Japan under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, following the signing of Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on 7th August 2025 and adoption of the Rule of Implementation (RoI) on 8th June 2026.

The development signals a transition from institutional preparation to implementation and establishes a clear, transparent and comprehensive procedural framework for implementing activities under India-Japan JCM. The manual provides detailed procedures covering the entire project cycle—from the submission of a Project Idea Note to the issuance and authorization of JCM credits.

2319367.title: Ministry of Textiles Organises Swachhta and Cleanliness Activities on Gandhi Jayanti under Special Campaign 6
2319367.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles Organises Swachhta and Cleanliness Activities on Gandhi Jayanti under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Textiles observed Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October 2026 with a series of Swachhta and cleanliness activities under Special Campaign 6.0, reaffirming its commitment to promoting cleanliness, hygiene and a culture of responsible workplace practices.

The programme was led by Secretary (Textiles) at the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Delhi, and was attended by senior officers of the Ministry of Textiles, faculty members and staff of NIFT Delhi. On the occasion, the Swachhta Pledge was administered, with participants reaffirming their commitment to maintaining cleanliness and contributing towards a cleaner and healthier environment.

A cleanliness drive was also undertaken at the NIFT Delhi campus, with active participation of officers, faculty and staff. The activities focused on improving cleanliness and upkeep of the premises, promoting proper waste management and sensitising participants towards maintaining clean and hygienic surroundings.

The observance of Gandhi Jayanti under Special Campaign 6 underscores the Ministry of Textiles’ continued efforts to institutionalise Swachhta in its offices and field establishments and to encourage collective participation in creating clean, well-maintained and sustainable workplaces. The Ministry continues to accord priority to cleanliness, disposal of obsolete and unusable items, better workplace management and sustained improvement in cleanliness standards as part of the Special Campaign.

Textile Waste Collection Drive starting this Gandhi Jayanti

As part of the initiative, starting this Gandhi Jayanti, 2nd October 2026, a dedicated textile waste collection bins have been installed at various locations. The initiative seeks to further strengthen the spirit of Jan Bhagidari and collective action towards a clean and sustainable India, with emphasis on cleanliness, responsible waste management, and the adoption of sustainable practices.

The initiative aims to promote responsible collection, segregation, recycling and upcycling of post-consumer textile waste and to encourage sustainable waste-management practices in Central Government office complexes and residential colonies in New Delhi. All officers and officials have been requested to actively participate in the drive by bringing and depositing their post-consumer textile waste in the designated collection bins during the campaign period

As part of the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6, Officers and employees of the attached and subordinate offices of Ministry of Textiles actively participated in the Swachhta Pledge, reaffirming their commitment towards cleanliness, hygiene and maintaining a clean and sustainable working environment.

          

As part of the campaign, a comprehensive cleanliness and de-cluttering drive was undertaken at the National Jute Board premises at Patsan Bhawan, Kolkata, and the Regional Office, New Delhi, from 2nd to 4th October 2026                     

Before                                                                                             After

The Ministry of Textiles continues to make concerted efforts towards achieving the objectives of Special Campaign 6, with a particular focus on Swachhta, cleanliness, space management, disposal of pending references and e-waste management.

2319355.title: CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana
2319355.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2319355.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has further intensified its coordinated field-level monitoring mechanism for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. As part of the monitoring mechanism, Flying Squads have been deployed in 34 districts across the two States for the period from 01.10.2026 to 30.11.2026, following a communication made by CAQM to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

 

CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. For more details, visit: https://t.co/u3EqSC98CP https://t.co/AIZp3UdZJL

— Commission for Air Quality Management (@CAQM_Official) October 5, 2026

 

Accordingly, Flying Squads have been deployed across the identified districts of Punjab and Haryana. The deployment covers 18 districts in Punjab and 16 districts in Haryana, providing extensive field-level monitoring across the two States during the critical paddy harvesting period.

The Flying Squads will assess the ground-level situation in their respective allocated districts and coordinate closely with the concerned authorities and field-level stakeholders for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning. The teams will coordinate with farmers, Parali Protection Force, district-level authorities, State Government Nodal Officers, officers of the respective State Pollution Control Boards, CAQM Cell at SAS Nagar and the Commission. The ground situation, along with the steps taken to prevent further incidents of paddy stubble burning, will be reported to the CAQM Cell on a daily basis.

The deployment has been structured in successive phases, with Flying Squads assigned to respective districts for different deployment periods to ensure sustained field-level monitoring throughout the paddy harvesting season 2026. The district-wise deployment covers key paddy-producing districts in Punjab, including Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Firozpur, Muktsar, Bathinda, Amritsar, Moga, Mansa, Fazilka, Patiala, Ludhiana, Kapurthala, Faridkot, Barnala, Malerkotla, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar and Fatehgarh Sahib. In Haryana, the deployment covers Jind, Fatehabad, Hisar, Kaithal, Sonipat, Rohtak, Sirsa, Karnal, Palwal, Jhajjar, Kurukshetra, Ambala, Yamunanagar, Faridabad, Panipat and Hansi.

The strengthened field-level mechanism is aimed at ensuring timely assessment of the on-ground situation, close coordination among enforcement agencies and prompt preventive action to tackle stubble burning incidents during the harvesting season. The daily field-level reports from the Flying Squads will also facilitate continuous assessment of the situation by the Commission and enable coordinated follow-up with the concerned authorities, wherever required.

CAQM has been continuously monitoring, coordinating and reviewing the implementation of measures for prevention of paddy stubble burning with the concerned State Governments, State Pollution Control Boards and District Administrations. The Commission has reiterated the need for concerted efforts by all concerned agencies, along with active facilitation and cooperation of farmers and other stakeholders, to ensure prevention of stubble burning during the season.
