2318441.title: 2.42 Lakh Special Gram Sabhas Across India Put Citizen-Centric Initiatives at the Heart of Grassroots Discussions on Gandhi Jayanti
2318441.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
2.42 Lakh Special Gram Sabhas Across India Put Citizen-Centric Initiatives at the Heart of Grassroots Discussions on Gandhi Jayanti
‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’ Gets Underway; Special Gram Sabhas Set the Stage for Panchayat Development Plans 2027-28
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country, with more than 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas scheduled on the GPDP Portal (https://gpdp.nic.in) and Panchayat NIRNAY Portal (https://meetingonline.gov.in). These Gram Sabhas witnessed enthusiastic and active participation of local residents, elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and officials. The Special Gram Sabhas also marked the commencement of the People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, under which Panchayats will prepare their Panchayat Development Plans for the Financial Year 2027-28. In these 2.42 lakh special Gram Sabhas, schemes and pioneering initiatives of the Government of India, namely from the Ministry of Panchayati Raj; the Department of Rural Development; the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation; the Department of Consumer Affairs; the Department of Food and Public Distribution; the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; and the Department of Land Resources were placed at the center of the discussions.

The Special Gram Sabhas provided rural citizens with a direct platform to participate in discussions on key government initiatives and issues of local relevance. The wide-ranging deliberations covered enhanced devolution of Central Finance Commission grants to Panchayats, financial self-reliance through Own Source Revenue, secure property and land rights, assured employment and livelihoods, safe drinking water and sanitation, water security, food security, consumer protection and women’s economic empowerment, among other areas. Agenda and awareness material highlighting key government initiatives, including transformative governance reforms and citizen-centric measures undertaken over the last twelve years, were read out and deliberated upon. Local residents, elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and officials actively participated, sharing their experiences, perspectives and suggestions, which will contribute to enriching the Gram Panchayat Development Plans. The nationwide conduct of these Special Gram Sabhas was supported by the coordinated efforts of partner Ministries and Departments, along with their field and grassroots-level functionaries and MY Bharat volunteers. Their engagement across State, District, Block and Gram Panchayat levels helped facilitate meaningful dialogue on citizen-centric schemes and initiatives, while strengthening Jan Bhagidari and Samvaad at the grassroots. Adopting a Whole-of-Government approach, Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, along with senior officers of the Ministry and participating Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, remained in continuous touch with officials of States and Union Territories throughout the day, reviewing the progress of Special Gram Sabhas across the country and facilitating close coordination in the spirit of cooperative federalism. The coordinated efforts of States and Union Territories, supported by their Panchayati Raj Departments, district administrations and field functionaries, ensured the seamless conduct of this nationwide exercise on an unprecedented scale.

People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27 ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’

The People’s Plan Campaign, led by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in collaboration with 21 Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, reflects the Whole-of-Government approach under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Ministry has been rolling out the People’s Plan Campaign in all States and Union Territories since 2018 to enable Panchayats to prepare evidence-based, holistic and participatory plans. Under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, the Ministry supports training and capacity building across nine themes of local development. More than 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats prepare participatory Gram Panchayat Development Plans and upload them on the eGramSwaraj portal, while the Panchayat Advancement Index helps each Gram Panchayat identify its achievements and gaps. On this basis, the Gram Sabha can take a Sankalp on priority areas, advancing the Localisation of Sustainable Development Goals and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Key reforms and achievements presented in the Special Gram Sabhas

Empowered and self-reliant Panchayats (Ministry of Panchayati Raj). The Sixteenth Finance Commission has recommended ₹4,35,236 crore for Rural Local Bodies for 2026-31, an increase of nearly 84 per cent over the Fifteenth Finance Commission, with the annual per capita grant rising from about ₹400 to nearly ₹950. The SAMARTH Panchayat Portal has registered over 57 lakh taxpayers and 15 lakh properties, and the Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award carries incentives of up to ₹1 crore. Panchayat accounts now follow the six-tier structure used by the Union and State Governments, and more than 2.5 lakh Panchayati Raj Institutions have joined the AuditOnline system. Under the Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA) Scheme, 3.33 crore property cards have been generated for 2.06 lakh villages, with loans of about ₹1,713 crore sanctioned and recognition of women as property owners encouraged.

Employment and livelihoods (Department of Rural Development). The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), in force since 1 July 2026, guarantees 125 days of wage employment every financial year to eligible rural households, with attendance through Face Authentication and digital payments. More than 31.69 crore person days have been generated, over 2.81 crore workers from about 2.23 crore households have received employment, and works are under way in nearly 2.31 lakh Gram Panchayats. An interim allocation of ₹93,841 crore has been made to States and Union Territories for 2026-27, and the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan enables the Gram Sabha to decide works according to local needs.

Safe drinking water and sanitation (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation). Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, rural tap water connections have grown from about 3.23 crore households (17 per cent) to more than 16 crore (over 80 per cent), and Jal Arpan, the handing over of completed water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and communities, was also highlighted. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), 12.22 crore household toilets have been built and over 5.25 lakh villages (89.6 per cent) have declared themselves Open Defecation Free Plus (Model). The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 were discussed during the gram sabhas, as Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 culminates.

Water security (Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation). Through Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain, more than 1.55 crore artificial recharge and storage structures have been constructed with community participation, and an impact study of the first phase estimated groundwater recharge of 2.43 billion cubic metres. Revised watershed development norms have raised funding to ₹22,000 per hectare in plain areas and ₹28,000 in hilly and difficult areas, and reduced the project period from seven to five years. The Gram Sabha activities under Catch the Rain focused on raising awareness about rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and community-led water conservation. Local communities, Panchayati Raj representatives and district officials participated actively in the programme, which featured technical guidance, screening of awareness videos, tree plantation and Shramdaan activities, along with the administration of the Jal Shapath. The Catch the Rain (CTR) Anthem was also played and displayed to reinforce the message of conserving every drop of rainwater and mobilising collective action towards sustainable water management.

Food security and consumer protection (Departments of Food and Public Distribution, and Consumer Affairs). Under One Nation One Ration Card, about 3.27 crore portability transactions take place every month, and the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to up to 81.35 crore beneficiaries, extended up to 2028. The National Consumer Helpline, available in 17 languages, received 3,42,371 calls in August 2026 against 78,477 in August 2019, and has facilitated refunds of over ₹105 crore since April 2025. The e-Jagriti platform has disposed of more than 2.55 lakh of 2.81 lakh cases instituted and received the Silver Award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026.

Digital land records (Department of Land Resources). Under the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme, 99.90 per cent of Records of Rights and 97.4 per cent of cadastral maps have been digitised. Citizens in 31 States and Union Territories can access land records online, and in 24 states/UTs can download digitally signed records, safeguarding owners against fraudulent mutations and facilitating access to credit.

Awareness on other key national initiatives

Several Ministries/Departments extended valuable support in ensuring awareness at the village level. The Ministry of Home Affairs facilitated awareness on the new criminal laws, namely the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam; the Ministry of Cooperation on the Digital Transformation and Strengthening of Cooperatives; the Ministry of Women and Child Development on Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat; and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, in pursuit of safe, healthy, child marriage free and drug free villages. These Special Gram Sabhas reaffirmed the Gram Sabha as the foundation of participatory democracy and local governance. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj looks forward to the preparation of people-centred Panchayat Development Plans for 2027-28 under the People’s Plan Campaign, towards building Sashakt, Atmanirbhar and Viksit Panchayats in the larger endeavour of Viksit Bharat.

2318389.title: "Context Matters, Care Matters, Compassion Matters": CEO BHASHINI at MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave
2318389.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
"Context Matters, Care Matters, Compassion Matters": CEO BHASHINI at MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave
Scientific Conclave on Digital Innovations in Nursing Practice held as part of MNS Centenary Year celebrations
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Military Nursing Service (MNS) organised the Scientific Conclave on “Digital Innovations in Nursing Practice: Harmonizing Technology with Compassionate Care” as part of the closing ceremony of its  Centenary Year 2026 at Manekshaw Centre, Delhi Cantt. The conclave brought together senior leadership, nursing professionals, healthcare practitioners and technology stakeholders to deliberate on the evolving role of digital innovation in strengthening healthcare delivery and nursing practice.

Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, BHASHINI, was invited as the Keynote Speaker at the inaugural ceremony of the Scientific Conclave, where he delivered a keynote address titled “Wired in Wellness: The Scope of Opportunities of Digital Health in Transforming the Healthcare Landscape.”

General Dhiraj Seth, PVSM, UYSM, AVSM, Chief of the Army Staff, was the Chief Guest for the inaugural ceremony. The programme also witnessed the release of the MNS Diary and the Nursing Research Compendium, along with the e-release of the scientific souvenir titled “Digital Pulse of Nursing: Connecting Technology, Transforming Care.”

In his keynote address, Shri Nag highlighted the transformative potential of digital technologies in healthcare, emphasising that language, context and healthcare-specific data are essential to building technology that is accessible, accurate and responsive to the needs of patients and healthcare professionals.

He outlined the four pillars of BHASHINI and its growing role in healthcare, including speech, translation and other language technologies, which can reduce communication barriers and make healthcare systems more inclusive across India's diverse linguistic landscape.

He stressed the need for medical and nursing glossaries as foundational language resources for healthcare-focused AI systems. While medical terminology requires consistency, patients often describe symptoms in everyday language, and the same condition may be expressed differently across languages, regions and contexts. AI systems therefore need healthcare-specific language data to understand this diversity accurately. A well-developed glossary can connect clinical terminology with everyday language, creating a common language layer between healthcare professionals, patients and AI systems.

Shri Nag also underlined the importance of language in care delivery. Since healthcare communication spans diverse linguistic and social contexts, language, datasets, digital literacy and clinical accuracy are key to the effective adoption of digital health technologies.

He spoke about the BHASHINI Domain Innovation Challenge in Healthcare, which encourages technology-led solutions to practical challenges in healthcare communication. Among the solutions highlighted was an AI-powered voice-to-text tool for OPD prescriptions, demonstrating how speech and language technologies can support clinical workflows and enable more efficient documentation. He noted the potential of voice-first and multilingual technologies to bridge the gap between technology and the realities of healthcare delivery, particularly where communication must move seamlessly between clinical terminology and the language patients use.

Speaking on language in compassionate healthcare, Shri Nag said, "Context matters, care matters, compassion matters, and healthcare, all three become even more important when we are communicating with people in a language they understand."

The discussions at the Scientific Conclave reflected the growing intersection of nursing, healthcare, digital technologies and AI, while underscoring the need to keep technological advancement grounded in the human dimensions of care.

The participation of CEO, BHASHINI, at the MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave highlighted the importance of building digital health solutions that recognise India's linguistic diversity and support healthcare professionals and patients through technologies that are accessible, context-aware and designed around real-world communication needs.

The Scientific Conclave formed an important part of the closing celebrations of the Centenary Year of the Military Nursing Service, commemorating a century of dedicated service and recognising the evolving role of nursing in an increasingly technology-enabled healthcare ecosystem.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, enabling greater accessibility to digital services through Language AI.

2318369.title: Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme:  Empowering Entrepreneurs and Driving Inclusive Growth Across India
2318369.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme:  Empowering Entrepreneurs and Driving Inclusive Growth Across India
Success Stories Reflect Transformational Impact of PMEGP on Livelihoods and Enterprise Growth
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

PMEGP, a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) plays a crucial role in promoting self-employment by enabling the establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. Under the scheme, prospective entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance in the form of Margin Money (MM) subsidy on bank-sanctioned loans providing much needed impetus to enterprise creation.

Since FY 2014-15, around 8.12 lakh micro entrepreneurs have been assisted with MM Subsidy to the tune of Rs. 24,398.61 crore under PMEGP for generation of sustainable employment opportunities to ~73.08 lakh persons.

Turning Aspirations into Enterprises: PMEGP Driving Grassroots Transformation

PMEGP is transforming the aspirations of ordinary individuals into successful enterprises by providing easy access to credit supported by MM subsidy. It enables first-generation entrepreneurs to establish viable businesses, turning job seekers into job creators.

The success of PMEGP is best reflected in the inspiring journeys of its beneficiaries, who have transformed their entrepreneurial aspirations into thriving enterprises:

Skinkaanti Ayurveda – From Micro Enterprise to National Leader: Founded by Smt. Pooja Sharma based in Parwanoo, Himachal Pradesh, Skinkaanti Ayurveda exemplifies remarkable growth from a modest micro-enterprise into India’s largest handmade soap manufacturing unit. Established with a project cost of Rs. 25 lakh and supported by State Bank of India, the enterprise today records an impressive annual turnover of Rs. 30 crore and provides employment to 300 individuals, of which 95% are women. By blending Ayurvedic principles with modern scientific techniques, the unit has achieved significant technological breakthroughs, including improved manufacturing efficiency and cost reduction, while supplying products across India through diverse retail and institutional channels.

M/s Ess Pee Quality Products – From PMEGP Support to Global Recognition: Established by Shri Surender Pal Singh Nagi in Mohali, Punjab, M/s Ess Pee Quality Products has evolved into a globally competitive food processing enterprise. With an initial project cost of Rs. 21 lakh financed by Bank of Baroda, the unit has grown into a Rs. 38 crore turnover business, generating employment for around 130 individuals. The enterprise manufactures honey, cookies, and fruit jams, and exports to 26 countries, including the USA, Australia, and France. Its achievement of the prestigious AA+ BRCGS certification highlights its adherence to global quality and safety standards.

The success stories of the PMEGP entrepreneurs demonstrate the transformative impact of the scheme in fostering entrepreneurship, promoting scaling up of micro-enterprises and a key driver of employment generation and inclusive growth across the country.

Prospective beneficiaries can know more about the scheme and submit their applications through the official PMEGP portal at: https://pmegp.msme.gov.in/

2318366.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
On the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary, Khadi and Village Industries Commission Chairman Shri Manoj Goyal launched nationwide discount on Khadi and Village Industries products.
New energy infused to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 'Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi' campaign
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi

Infusing  new energy to the call of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for 'Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi' and 'Vocal for Local', Shri Manoj Goyal, Chairman,  Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, purchased Khadi products at Gramodyog Bhawan, Gram Shilpa Emporium and launched nationwide special discount sale. On this occasion, he purchased Khadi and Village Industries products and made digital payments through UPI. Many dignitaries shopped at the showroom at Connaught Place on Gandhi Jayanti. Addressing the media on the occasion, Chairman KVIC Shri Manoj Goyal said that KVIC is making continuous efforts to take Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's call of 'Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi' to the masses and Gen-Z.

Chairman KVIC informed that on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, a special discount campaign has been launched across the country including Khadi Bhawan at Connaught Place in New Delhi. The discount will be available from October 2 to November 16, 2026. During this period, up to 20 per cent discount will be available on Khadi products and 10 per cent discount on village industry products. He further reiterated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Khadi has attained a new dimension. Today, Khadi is becoming a powerful medium to realize the resolutions of Atmanirbhar Bharat, Vocal for Local, Local to Global and Developed India-2047. He said that Khadi is not just a apparel, but the livelihood of crores of artisans and weavers, the cultural heritage of India and a symbol of sustainable development.

Shri Goyal speaking on this occasion said that as a result of the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and Village Industries sector has also made unprecedented progress. The turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector stood at over Rs 1.87 lakh crore in the financial year 2025-26, while more than 2.04 crore people are getting employment through this sector. He expressed confidence that the sector will also achieve the turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore in the coming time.

2318364.title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar And Shri B. L. Verma Distribute 662 Aids, Assistive Devices Costing Over ₹10 Lakh Distributed To 114 Senior Citizens In Delhi-NCR Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana
2318364.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar And Shri B. L. Verma Distribute 662 Aids, Assistive Devices Costing Over ₹10 Lakh Distributed To 114 Senior Citizens In Delhi-NCR Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana
Government Reiterates Commitment To Ensuring Dignity, Independence And Quality Of Life For Senior Citizens
Dr Virendra Kumar Calls For Collective Efforts To Ensure Senior Citizens Live Their Life With Dignity, Respect And Honour
Shri B. L. Verma Lauds  Invaluable Contribution And Sacrifices Of Senior Citizens In The Nation-Building Process
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, organised a distribution programme under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital here today.

During the programme, 662 aids and assistive devices, costing over ₹10 lakh, were distributed to 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizen Homes across Delhi-NCR.

The aids and assistive devices were distributed by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, and Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment.

 

Shri Sajeesh Kumar N., Joint Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri Praveen Kumar, Chairman and Managing Director, Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), were also present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar recalled that the International Day of Older Persons was observed across the country yesterday (October 1, 2026) and aids and assistive devices were distributed to 904 senior citizens at Bhavnagar, Gujarat on the occasion. He appreciated the contribution of youth, NGOs and civil society organizations in facilitating such initiatives and supporting senior citizens.

Dr. Virendra Kumar observed that senior citizens often experience difficulties relating to hearing, mobility and vision with advancing age. He stated that the Ministry has decided to expand the distribution of assistive devices to beneficiaries residing in Senior Citizens’ Homes across the country, in consonance with the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on the completion of 25 years in governance.

The Minister emphasized that access to appropriate assistive devices can help senior citizens become more self-reliant in carrying out their daily activities and lead their lives with greater dignity and confidence.

Highlighting the significant contributions made by senior citizens in diverse fields, including agriculture, literature and the armed forces, Dr. Virendra Kumar noted that many elderly persons also face challenges arising from loneliness and social isolation. He emphasized the need for collective efforts to ensure that senior citizens are able to live their lives with dignity, respect and honour.

He called upon youth, corporates, NGOs and organizations working for the welfare of senior citizens to come forward and contribute towards building an inclusive society, in keeping with the vision of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas outlined by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Dr. Virendra Kumar further noted that, according to Census 2011, India has 10.38 crore senior citizens, with approximately 70 per cent residing in rural areas. Emphasising the Government’s efforts to improve accessibility to welfare services, he stated that the Ministry plans to increase the number of PM-Divya Asha Kendras from 109 to 300 so that senior citizens can access assistive devices and related services more conveniently and without undue waiting.

Addressing the gathering, Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, welcomed the senior citizens and highlighted the importance of the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, launched by the Department on April 1, 2017, under the guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister to benefit senior citizens in need of aids and assistive devices.

Shri B. L. Verma lauded the invaluable contributions and sacrifices made by senior citizens in the nation-building process. He also highlighted the initiatives being undertaken by the Department to promote inter-generational bonding and reduce the generation gap, while ensuring greater social inclusion and participation of senior citizens.

Shri Verma expressed the hope that senior citizens across the country would continue to contribute their experience, knowledge and wisdom towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Shri Praveen Kumar, Chairman and Managing Director, ALIMCO, highlighted the performance and efficiency of ALIMCO in implementing the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana under the guidance of Dr. Virendra Kumar. He also underscored the use of Artificial Intelligence by ALIMCO to better serve senior citizens in the coming years.

The programme concluded with the Hon’ble Ministers, along with the invited senior citizens, offering floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi , Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri & Dr B R Ambedkar.

The programme reflects the Government’s continued commitment towards ensuring the dignity, independence and well-being of senior citizens, while strengthening access to aids and assistive devices and enabling them to lead a more self-reliant and dignified life.

The programme reflects the Government’s continued commitment to promoting the dignity, independence, inclusion and well-being of senior citizens. Through initiatives such as the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, the Government is strengthening access to assistive devices and enabling senior citizens, particularly those in need, to lead more independent, self reliant, dignified and fulfilling lives.

It is pertinent to mention that Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) is an initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at providing physical aids and assisted-living devices to senior citizens in need, thereby supporting their mobility, independence and quality of life. The programme seeks to facilitate greater social inclusion and enable senior citizens to participate more independently in everyday life.

2318358.title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 in New Delhi
2318358.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 in New Delhi
Nar Seva is Narayana Seva;Service to Society is Nation-Building at the Grassroots: Vice-President
Viksit Bharat Must Be Built on Compassion, Character and Social Responsibility: Vice-President
Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, Nasha Mukt Bharat Roadmap Important Initiatives for Drug-Free India: Vice-President
Vice-President Calls for Strengthening Spirit of Seva Bhav and Kartavya Bodh Among Youth
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 as the Chief Guest in New Delhi and presented the Sant Eshwar Seva Samman to individuals and organisations recognised for their exemplary and selfless service to society.

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the Sant Eshwar Samman is a recognition of the spirit of selfless service and a celebration of India’s culture of compassion and responsibility. He extended his greetings and congratulations to all the awardees for their extraordinary contributions to the nation.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the Sant Eshwar Foundation and Rashtriya Sewa Bharati for instituting the awards and sustaining the initiative for 11 consecutive years. He said that by recognising countless individuals who work silently to strengthen society and make the nation more inclusive, the awards motivate others to follow the path of Seva.

Highlighting the timeless Indian tradition of service, the Vice-President said, “Our civilisational ethos has always taught us, ‘Nar Seva is Narayana Seva’.” He noted that the great saints and thinkers of Bharat have inspired people to rise above narrow boundaries of self and dedicate themselves to the welfare of others.

Referring to the goal of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Vice-President emphasised that development cannot be measured only through economic growth, infrastructure or technological advancement. A truly developed India, he said, is one where every citizen experiences dignity, opportunity and hope.

He said that every citizen is a stakeholder in the nation’s progress and that the work of service organisations and individuals constitutes nation-building at the grassroots. Citing the Swachh Bharat Mission as an example, he said the initiative demonstrated how Jan Bhagidari can transform a government programme into a people’s movement.

The Vice-President also highlighted the serious threat posed by narcotic drugs and substance abuse to the health and future of the youth. He recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan in August this year, while Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah launched the Nasha Mukt Bharat 2029 Roadmap. He said that both initiatives are important steps towards building a drug-free India.

Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for development to be accompanied by compassion, character and social responsibility, and congratulated all the awardees. He expressed the hope that their lives would inspire more citizens, particularly the youth, to dedicate themselves to the welfare of society and strengthen the spirit of Seva Bhav and Kartavya Bodh.

2318353.title: CAQM Reviews Enforcement Status Across NCR; 197 Inspections Conducted in 17 Days
2318353.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2318353.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM Reviews Enforcement Status Across NCR; 197 Inspections Conducted in 17 Days
Commission’s Flying Squads carried out inspections at 28,744 units/projects/entities across NCR so far
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi

The 140th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 01.10.2026 to review enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period 08.09.2026 to 24.09.2026.

 

140th Meeting of Enforcement Task Force (ETF) reviews enforcement actions, compliance status and inspections across NCR.

For more details, visit: https://t.co/HtYWEMQFN5 pic.twitter.com/S2l5uBGLrd

— Commission for Air Quality Management (@CAQM_Official) October 2, 2026

 

During the 17-day reporting period, a total of 197 inspections were reported, comprising 10 inspections at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites, 111 inspections in the Industrial Sector and 76 inspections related to Diesel Generator (DG) sets. The industrial sector inspections included 22 inspections conducted as part of a special inspection drive. Based on the inspections, violations were reported in 85 cases, comprising 8 C&D cases, 49 industrial cases and 28 DG-related cases.

As per the violations reported by the concerned sectors, various enforcement actions have been proposed. These include closure of 4 C&D projects and 1 industrial unit; sealing of 28 DG sets; issuance of orders/directions for compliance in 17 cases, including 4 DG sets; and Environmental Compensation (EC) in 10 cases. Other proposed actions include issuance of letters to project proponents, re-inspection, forwarding of cases to CPCB/SPCB, advisories and other appropriate follow-up measures.

The ETF was apprised of the action taken during the special inspection drive conducted in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh on 15.09.2026 by 7 teams of the Flying Squads of the Commission, along with District Administration and Police personnel and officers of UPPCB. A total of 22 premises were inspected, of which 05 were found compliant and 1 had already been sealed by UPPCB. The actions suggested in the remaining cases include closure of 4 units, sealing of 1 DG set, issuance of orders in 5 cases, imposition of EC in 4 cases, and re-inspection and prosecution in 2 cases.

The status of resumption orders issued after the previous ETF meeting was also reviewed. As on 30.09.2026, a total of 9 resumption orders had been issued, comprising 2 industrial units and 7 C&D sites. State-wise, 1 resumption order was issued in Delhi, 3 in Haryana and 5 in Uttar Pradesh. Further, 1 case was transferred to the concerned State Pollution Control Board for final decision, pertaining to an industrial unit in Uttar Pradesh.

The updated cumulative enforcement status as on 01.10.2026 was also reviewed. It was noted that the Flying Squads of the Commission have so far carried out inspections at 28,744 units/projects/entities across NCR. Based on these inspections, 1,831 Closure Directions have been issued, out of which 1,488 Resumption Orders have been issued after verification of compliance. Further, 127 cases have been transferred to the respective State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) for final decision, while 216 entities remain for issuance of resumption orders.

In addition, a special inspection drive of industrial units in Loni, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh was conducted on 29.09.2026 by 7 inspection teams to assess compliance with applicable environmental norms and directions of the Commission. A total of 21 units/ locations were inspected and all 21 were found non-compliant. The major non-compliances observed included operation of furnaces without adequate stack/chimney and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), operation without valid Consent to Operate (CTO), operation of industrial units in non-conforming areas, use of unapproved fuel including coal, operation of pit furnaces without stack, APCD and OCEMS, non-compliance related to DG sets, and waste processing activities without CTO and adequate APCDs. In some previously sealed premises, indications of continued operation, including sounds of metal activity and/or smoke emissions, were also observed. Necessary corrective action(s) have been directed.

The Commission reiterated the need for continued strengthening of enforcement, timely verification of compliance and close coordination among implementing agencies for effective implementation of the prescribed norms. The Commission also emphasized expeditious enforcement action, strict compliance monitoring and continued inspections across priority sectors, including Industrial Units, C&D activities and DG sets, to ensure effective mitigation of air pollution across the NCR.

2318348.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment takes “Shram Samvad” outreach to industrial clusters in Delhi, Haryana and Uttarakhand
2318348.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Ministry of Labour & Employment takes “Shram Samvad” outreach to industrial clusters in Delhi, Haryana and Uttarakhand
District-level programmes held in Haridwar, Naraina and Sonipat on Labour Codes, employer compliance, PMVBRY and social security
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, continued its nationwide “Shram Samvad” initiative with District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes held on October 1, 2026 at Haridwar in Uttarakhand, Naraina Industrial Area in New Delhi and Sonipat in Haryana. The programmes brought together government officials, industry associations, employers, HR and legal professionals and other stakeholders to enhance awareness of the four Labour Codes, employer compliance requirements and key employment and social-security initiatives of the Government.

The Shram Samvad campaign, launched nationwide on September 28, 2026, is a 90-day outreach initiative under which the Ministry is undertaking district-level engagement across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories, with a focus on industrial clusters. The initiative seeks to provide employers and other stakeholders with greater clarity on the provisions, applicability and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes and facilitate effective implementation at the ground level.

At Haridwar, the programme was organised in partnership with SCOPE at the BHEL Admin Building. Around 125 participants, including representatives of industry associations and business establishments, employers, industrialists, professionals and officials from EPFO, ESIC and the Central Labour Commissioner’s office, participated in the programme. Shri Govind Ram, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, provided an overview of the four Labour Codes and the basic employer compliance chain, including establishment and workforce parameters, applicability thresholds and principal compliance areas. Shri Venkanna Banothu, Director of Mines Safety, DGMS, and senior representatives of the Uttarakhand Labour Department also participated.

At Naraina Industrial Area, New Delhi, the programme was organised in collaboration with Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and Naraina Industries Association and was attended by around 80 participants representing employers, industry, HR, legal and finance professionals and other stakeholders. Shri Ashok Kumar Singh, IAS, Director General, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), delivered the keynote address, highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes and the importance of stakeholder awareness, compliance readiness and effective implementation.

At Sonipat, the Ministry organised the Shram Samvad programme in collaboration with Laghu Udyog Bharati at Wyndham Garden. The programme witnessed participation of around 70 stakeholders, including employers, State authorities and representatives from the labour and employment ecosystem. Shri P.B. Verma, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), delivered the inaugural address. The technical sessions included an overview of the new Labour Codes by Shri Minhaz Ahmed, Director, Ministry of Labour & Employment.

Across the three programmes, technical discussions covered the Code on Wages, 2019; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Code on Social Security, 2020; and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Dedicated sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) were also conducted.

Senior officials and representatives of EPFO, ESIC and the Central Labour Commissioner’s Office actively participated in the programmes across all venues. A key component of the programmes was the interactive Question-and-Answer sessions, enabling participants to raise practical issues concerning applicability, statutory compliance, records and returns, employee benefits and implementation of the new framework. The sessions provided stakeholders with an opportunity to seek clarifications directly from officials of the Ministry and its attached and subordinate offices.

2318321.title: India and Netherlands Discuss Deepening Agricultural Cooperation
2318321.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
India and Netherlands Discuss Deepening Agricultural Cooperation
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan holds talks with Dutch Minister Mr. Silvio Erkens; discussions focus on Centres of Excellence, seed sector cooperation, market access issues and agricultural innovation
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, held bilateral talks with Mr. Silvio Erkens, Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, Netherlands, in New Delhi on 28th September 2026.

The meeting focused on reviewing ongoing cooperation in agriculture sector, and strengthening agricultural cooperation by exploring new areas of cooperation. Both sides reiterated their resolve to enhance productivity through modern technology, innovation and knowledge exchange.

Both sides discussed progress on establishment of 25 Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in the agriculture and horticulture sectors. Further, both sides agreed to explore cooperation in the seed sector though a work plan outlining key areas of cooperation for a clear framework for effective implementation.

In the area of agricultural innovation, both sides discussed identifying potential areas of cooperation, recognising the significant progress and advancements made by both countries in this field.

In addition to the Agriculture Minister, the Dutch delegation included Mr. Marten van den Berg, Director General, and other senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, along with Ms. Marisa Gerards, Ambassador, and other officials from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in India.

The Indian side included Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Dr. M L Jat, Secretary, DARE and other senior officials of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

2318302.title: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Mourns the Untimely Demise of Dr. Engam Pame (IIS), ADG, Shri Nampibou Marinmai (IIS), Director and Shri H. Lianvela, MTS
2318302.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Mourns the Untimely Demise of Dr. Engam Pame (IIS), ADG, Shri Nampibou Marinmai (IIS), Director and Shri H. Lianvela, MTS
The Officials Lose Their Lives in a Tragic Road Accident While on Official Duty in Mizoram
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting deeply mourns the untimely demise of three members of the Information and Broadcasting fraternity who lost their lives in a tragic road accident in Mizoram on October 1, 2026. The vehicle carrying the officials fell into a gorge while they were on official duty.

The deceased are Dr. Engam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau and Central Bureau of Communication, Imphal; Shri Nampibou Marinmai, IIS, Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl; and Shri H. Lianvela, MTS, Central Bureau of Communication, Field Office, Aizawl.

The tragic loss of three colleagues has deeply saddened the Ministry. Their untimely demise is a profound loss to their respective organisations and to the larger family of officials and professionals engaged in public communication and information dissemination across the country.

Dr. Engam Pame, 58, joined the Indian Information Service in 1994 after completing his MA in International Relations from the School of Social Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. During his more than three decades of service, he served in various capacities in Delhi, Imphal, Pune and Shillong, contributing to government communication, media coordination and public outreach.

As Additional Director General, PIB Imphal, Dr. Pame played an important role in strengthening communication and coordination with media organisations and government departments across the Northeast. One of the longest-serving Information Service Group A officers from the Northeast, he brought extensive field experience and a deep understanding of the region’s diverse communication landscape to his assignments. Dr. Pame belonged to the Zeme Naga community of Tamenglong district, Manipur. He is survived by his wife, Ajuna Pame, and a son and daughter.

Shri Nampibou Marinmai was an Indian Information Service officer and was serving as Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl. He was also Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC). He had earlier served as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, where he was associated with defence-related public relations, media reporting and communication.

Through his long association with news and public broadcasting, Shri Nampi made valuable contributions to public communication and information dissemination. His experience in defence public relations and broadcasting enabled him to facilitate communication between institutions and the media. His professional commitment, dedicated service and cordial association with colleagues and media professionals will be remembered with respect. He is survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Shri H. Lianvela, MTS, CBC Field Office Aizawl, had joined government service in 1998. He was 52 and is survived by his wife, daughter and grandson.

Shri Gojendra Dey, Driver, CBC, Field Office, Aizawl, also sustained injuries in the accident and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. He is conscious and under medical care.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting stands with the bereaved families, colleagues and friends of the three officials in this hour of profound grief. Their years of dedicated service to the Government and their contribution to public communication will be remembered with respect and gratitude.

***

2318261.title: Historic First for Jammu & Kashmir (UT): Mining Development Begins with Successful Auction of Two Mineral Blocks
2318261.body_html:
Ministry of Mines
Historic First for Jammu & Kashmir (UT): Mining Development Begins with Successful Auction of Two Mineral Blocks
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

In a historic first, two mineral blocks in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir (UT) have been successfully auctioned through the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Central Government’s mineral auction process. The successful auction marks an important step towards unlocking the mineral potential of Jammu & Kashmir and initiating a new phase of organised mineral development in the Union Territory.

The development comes as Jammu & Kashmir continues to witness greater focus on infrastructure, investment and economic development following the abrogation of Article 370. The auction of these mineral blocks adds a new dimension to this development journey by enabling systematic exploration and development of the Union Territory’s mineral resources.

The Government of Jammu & Kashmir (UT) had entrusted the auction of mineral blocks to the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. The successful completion of the auction reflects the use of a transparent and competitive mineral auction process for the systematic development of mineral resources.

Details of the Blocks

Koot–Kapran Limestone Block, Anantnag

Located in Koot and Kapran villages of Dooru Tehsil in Anantnag district, the Koot–Kapran Limestone Block covers 22.43 hectares and has estimated limestone resources of 4.75 million tonnes. The block has been explored up to the G-4 stage, providing scope for further detailed exploration and development.

Wantrag Limestone Block, Anantnag

The Wantrag Limestone Block covers 5.36 hectares and has estimated limestone resources of 10.853 million tonnes. The block has been explored up to the G-3 stage, including 159 metres of drilling, providing an important geological basis for further exploration and development.

The auction of the two limestone blocks is expected to catalyse new investment and economic activity in the Union Territory. As mining and associated activities develop, they are expected to generate a large number of direct and indirect employment opportunities and create avenues for local businesses, entrepreneurs, service providers and allied industries.

The development of the mineral sector will also contribute to greater value creation from Jammu & Kashmir’s mineral resources and support new opportunities for local participation in the emerging mining ecosystem. This marks another step towards strengthening the economic foundations of a Viksit Jammu & Kashmir.

The Ministry of Mines will continue to work in coordination with the Government of Jammu & Kashmir to facilitate transparent, sustainable and responsible development of the Union Territory’s mineral resources.

2318247.title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches 'Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0'  Across Personnel, Science & Technology and Earth Sciences Ministries, Expanding Swachhata into a Wider Movement of Efficiency and Resource Management
2318247.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2318247.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches 'Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0'  Across Personnel, Science & Technology and Earth Sciences Ministries, Expanding Swachhata into a Wider Movement of Efficiency and Resource Management
 
Swachhata Evolves from Cleanliness Drive into Sustained Culture of Good Governance, Resource Optimisation and Public Service: Dr. Jitendra Singh 
₹5,102.91 Crore Generated from E-Waste and Scrap Disposal; Over 1,049 Lakh Sq. Ft. Office Space Freed in Five Years, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh 
Campaign Taken Forward at DoPT-DARPG, CSIR Headquarters and Ministry of Earth Sciences; Over 100 Science Institutions Join the Drive
CSIR’s Waste-to-Wealth Technologies Take Waste Management Beyond Disposal to Resource Recovery, Innovation and Value Creation
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

Swachhata has evolved from an appeal for cleanliness into a sustained culture of good governance, efficient utilisation of public resources, reduction of pendency and responsible management of waste, said Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, While launching the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 today.

Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for Swachhata from the Red Fort in 2014, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the initiative gradually transformed into a people’s movement and subsequently became an institutional practice across Government offices. He said the campaign has continuously acquired new dimensions, from toilets and cleanliness to disposal of old files, redundant furniture, e-files and electronic scrap, thereby linking Swachhata with administrative efficiency, optimum use of public space and productive management of resources.

Dr. Jitendra Singh began the day by participating in the launch activities of Special Campaign 6.0 at the venue designated by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). He participated in Shramdaan, plantation under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, and the symbolic commencement of weeding out old records, besides honouring Safai Mitras by distributing safety kits and sweets.

Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG; Smt. Rachna Shah, Secretary, DoPT; and Dr. Surendrakumar Bagde, Director General, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), were among the senior officers present. DARPG is the nodal department for the Special Campaign.

The Minister thereafter proceeded to CSIR Headquarters, where he took forward Special Campaign 6.0 across the scientific and technological ecosystem. Dr. Jitendra Singh led a mass cleanliness drive, participated in the Swachhata Signature Campaign and plantation drive, and felicitated Safai Mitras. Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR; Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology (DST); and Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), along with senior officials from DST, DBT and CSIR, participated in the programme. The activities at CSIR included review and disposal of obsolete records and scrap, workplace improvement and effective management of office spaces, with emphasis on Jan Bhagidari.

Speaking during the launch activities, Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled how the Swachhata movement, after its initial focus on sanitation, gradually entered Government offices and addressed the large accumulation of files and records that were no longer required but continued to occupy valuable space. He recalled that the exercise subsequently evolved into a dedicated annual campaign from 2 October to 31 October, with each successive campaign adding new dimensions. From physical files and discarded furniture, the exercise has expanded to e-files and e-scrap, reflecting the changing nature of Government workplaces and the growing need for responsible management of electronic assets.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the experience of the Special Campaigns has demonstrated that systematic disposal of redundant material can create both financial value for the public exchequer and usable space for Government offices. Over the last five years, ₹5,102.91 crore has been generated through disposal of e-waste and scrap, while more than 1,049.54 lakh square feet of office space has been cleared and put to productive use. More than 180.48 lakh files have also been closed or weeded out and 24.20 lakh cleanliness sites identified and cleaned across the country.

The Minister said the space released through the campaign can subsequently be put to productive use, including creation of green areas and restoration of spaces that had remained blocked or underutilised. He said the annual campaign serves as a renewed commitment to a practice that should continue throughout the year, while the repeated campaigns have helped make Swachhata part of the working culture of Government institutions.

The Minister subsequently visited the Ministry of Earth Sciences, where e-waste and obsolete equipment from Prithvi Bhavan and Mausam Bhavan were taken up for disposal under Special Campaign 6.0. Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, was present during the programme and briefed the Minister on the items identified for disposal.

The inventory comprises 705 items in all. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the exercise at the Ministry of Earth Sciences is part of a wider campaign across the scientific ecosystem, with similar activities being undertaken by institutions under Earth Sciences, CSIR and DST. He said more than 100 science institutions have commenced the campaign from 2 October, taking the message of Swachhata and responsible disposal of obsolete material across the country's scientific institutions.

The Minister also connected the campaign with the larger Waste-to-Wealth dimension of India's scientific ecosystem, where the objective goes beyond disposal of waste to developing technologies that can convert waste into useful products, materials, energy and new economic opportunities. The CSIR portfolio includes technologies for municipal solid-waste management, recycling of plastic waste, recovery of critical metals and rare earth elements from e-waste, recycling of lithium-ion batteries, biomethanation, conversion of agro-waste into biodegradable products, wastewater resource recovery and utilisation of industrial waste for value-added products. These technologies have been transferred to industry and other organisations for application and further development.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the experience of Special Campaigns demonstrates how a cleanliness initiative can progressively become an instrument of administrative reform, resource optimisation and institutional efficiency. In the scientific ecosystem, this approach is being extended further through technologies that enable waste to move through a larger value chain, from identification and disposal to recovery, recycling, innovation and wealth creation.

The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 will run from 2 October to 31 October 2026, following the preparatory phase undertaken by Ministries and Departments during September. The campaign focuses on Swachhata, reduction of pendency, review and weeding of records, efficient utilisation of office space, scientific disposal of e-waste and redundant material, and improved record management across Government offices. The campaign is being implemented as a whole-of-government effort, with institutional goals across Ministries and Departments.

2318243.title: Robotics to Become an Accelerating Tool in Every Specialty of Medicine: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
2318243.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Robotics to Become an Accelerating Tool in Every Specialty of Medicine: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
Robotics, AI and Nanoscience to Create Larger Ecosystem for Precision Health Delivery and Precision Medicine: Dr. Jitendra Singh 
From Robotic Surgery to Robotic Medicine, Technology Will Find Applications Across Medical Specialties, says Dr. Jitendra Singh 
Dr. Jitendra Singh: Tele-Robotics Can Take Specialist Expertise to the Patient Across Geographical Boundaries 
AI and Robotics Can Help India Address Its Unique and Diverse Healthcare Challenges, Says Union Minster Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, who is also a noted Physician and diabetologist, today said robotics is set to become an accelerating tool in every specialty of medicine, covering diagnostics as well as treatment and therapy.

He said robotics, together with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and nanoscience, would create a larger ecosystem for precision health delivery and precision medicine, with emerging technologies enabling increasingly personalised healthcare based on an individual’s genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns.

Dr. Jitendra Singh was delivering inaugural address at the International Conference of the "Society of Robotic Surgery" here. He said robotics should not be viewed as a technology confined to surgery but as a tool that would increasingly become part of different branches of medicine. “It’s a tool. It will happen everywhere,” he said, adding that while the present conference is focused on robotic surgery, the future could see the emergence of robotic medicine, robotic endocrinology and robotic cardiology, just as AI is finding applications across different medical specialties.

The Minister said medicine is entering an exciting phase of frontier practices, with the 21st century witnessing the emergence of AI, biotechnology, nuclear medicine and other technology-driven solutions. He said the next phase would see greater application of genetically driven diagnostic solutions, alongside advances in quantum technologies, nanomedicine and robotics.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said precision medicine would increasingly require treatment approaches tailored to individual patients, even when they are diagnosed with the same disease. Genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns, he said, would increasingly shape medical decision-making, making technology-enabled and personalised healthcare an important part of the future of medicine.

Referring to the Genome India Programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said 10,000 individuals have already been sequenced and expressed the hope that India could eventually move towards gene sequencing for every newborn. He said undertaking such detailed genetic sequencing for a population of 1.4 billion would require the optimal use of AI and robotics.

The Minister also spoke about the potential of nanomedicine in addressing longstanding healthcare challenges. Referring to efforts towards developing oral insulin, he said advances at the nano level could help overcome limitations associated with conventional drug delivery and open new possibilities for therapeutic interventions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s size, diversity and geographical spread make technologies such as AI, robotics and tele-robotics particularly relevant for healthcare delivery. Sharing his experience with robotic ultrasonography, he said he had performed an ultrasound on a person located 10,000 kilometres away in Antarctica, demonstrating the possibilities of remotely enabled medical technologies.

Describing the potential transformation in the traditional model of specialist healthcare, Dr. Jitendra Singh said, “Instead of the patient being referred to the doctor, it will be the doctor being referred to the patient.” He said tele-robotics could enable specialist expertise to reach patients across geographical boundaries, allowing advanced medical capabilities to be delivered without the patient necessarily having to travel to the specialist.

The Minister also spoke about India’s evolving disease profile, where infectious diseases continue to coexist with metabolic and lifestyle-related disorders. He said diseases traditionally associated with later stages of life are increasingly being seen among younger people, creating a complex healthcare landscape that requires both advanced technological tools and a more integrated and holistic approach.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the scale and diversity of India’s healthcare requirements make the adoption of new technologies particularly important. AI and robotics can serve as powerful facilitatory tools for health delivery across the country, while also supporting the transition towards precision and personalised medicine.

Dr. Jitendra Singh congratulated the organisers of SRS India 2026 for bringing robotic surgery into the domain of institutional learning, academics and professional conference platforms. He said the adoption of emerging technologies such as robotics would be essential to keep pace with the rapidly evolving landscape of medical science.

***

2318239.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Leads Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam Tree Plantation Drive At Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation; Hon’ble Minister Of State For Social Justice And Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma Joins The Drive
Plantation Drive Organised as Part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign to Promote a Clean and Green Environment
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment organised a tree plantation activity under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative at the Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation (BJRNF) in National Capital here today.

The plantation drive was led by Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, in the presence of Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Dr. Virendra Kumar led the tree plantation activity along with officials of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation.

Drawing a parallel between the nurturing of nature by Mother Earth and the nurturing of human life by mothers, Dr Kumar emphasised the importance of protecting and nurturing the environment.

The Officers and officials of the Ministry and BJRNF actively participated in the plantation drive, reaffirming their collective commitment towards environmental conservation and the creation of a clean and green environment.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Virendra Kumar highlighted the vision behind the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam initiative, which was initiated by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Dr. Virendra Kumar called upon all participants to contribute towards keeping Mother Earth Clean And Healthy, emphasising that collective efforts towards environmental conservation will help create a healthier and more sustainable environment for generations to come.

On the occasion, Dr. Virendra Kumar and Shri B. L. Verma paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. The dignitaries also paid their respects to Babu Jagjivan Ram.

Dr Virendra Kumar also administered a pledge to the officers and participants to contribute towards a clean and green environment.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the plantation drive reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and the broader vision of Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

He said the initiative also highlights the importance of nurturing urban green spaces and encouraging collective participation in environmental conservation.

The Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam plantation activity reinforces the message of environmental responsibility and sustainable development, while encouraging citizens and institutions to contribute towards building a cleaner, greener and healthier India.

2318085.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan pays tributes to Mahatma Gandhi Ji, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji and Thiru K. Kamaraj Ji
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today paid floral tributes and offered homage to Mahatma Gandhi Ji, former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Thiru K. Kamaraj Ji.

Paid tributes to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi Ji, at Rajghat on his birth anniversary. His unwavering faith in truth and non-violence, steadfast commitment to justice, and profound belief in the dignity of every individual continue to inspire humanity. Mahatma Gandhi Ji’s life and message remain an enduring beacon of peace, compassion, selflessness and service. On this solemn occasion, let us reaffirm our commitment to the values he cherished and dedicate ourselves to building a just, harmonious and inclusive society.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

At Raj Ghat, the Vice-President paid floral tributes and offered homage to Mahatma Gandhi Ji on his birth anniversary. Recalling his enduring legacy, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that Mahatma Gandhi Ji’s unwavering faith in truth and non-violence, steadfast commitment to justice and profound belief in the dignity of every individual continue to inspire humanity.

He said that Mahatma Gandhi Ji’s life and message remain an enduring beacon of peace, compassion, selflessness and service. He called upon everyone to reaffirm their commitment to the values cherished by Mahatma Gandhi Ji and dedicate themselves to building a just, harmonious and inclusive society.

Paid tributes to former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji on his birth anniversary at Vijay Ghat today. A leader of quiet strength and extraordinary resolve, Shastri Ji exemplified humility, integrity and an unwavering commitment to the nation. At a defining moment in India’s journey, his leadership instilled confidence and unity, while his call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” gave enduring recognition to the sacrifices of our soldiers and the vital contribution of our farmers. His life remains a powerful reminder that true leadership is rooted in simplicity, courage and service to the nation.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

At Vijay Ghat, the Vice-President paid floral tributes and offered homage to former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji on his birth anniversary.

Describing Shastri Ji as a leader of quiet strength and extraordinary resolve, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he exemplified humility, integrity and unwavering commitment to the nation. He recalled that, at a defining moment in India’s journey, Shastri Ji’s leadership instilled confidence and unity, while his call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” gave enduring recognition to the sacrifices of the nation’s soldiers and the vital contribution of its farmers.

The Vice-President said that Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji’s life remains a powerful reminder that true leadership is rooted in simplicity, courage and service to the nation.

A towering statesman and a true people’s leader, Kamaraj Ji devoted his life to the service of the nation and the welfare of the common people. His transformative contribution to education, particularly in expanding opportunities for children from underprivileged backgrounds, remains a defining legacy of his public life. His dedication to public welfare and his selfless approach to public life continue to inspire generations.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

2318074.title: Department of Pharmaceuticals Commences Special Campaign 6 with Focus on Scientific E-Waste Management and Pendency Liquidation
2318074.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2318074.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Department of Pharmaceuticals Commences Special Campaign 6 with Focus on Scientific E-Waste Management and Pendency Liquidation
12,208 Cleanliness Drives and 1,011 E-Waste Items Targeted Under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 11:54AM by PIB Delhi

In pursuance of the guidelines issued by the Government, the Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), along with its attached and subordinate organizations - including the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs), and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) - officially commenced Special Campaign 6, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, on October 2, 2026.

Following an intensive Preparatory Phase (September 15–30, 2026) where baseline targets, site identifications, and record inventories were successfully completed, the Department has now transitioned into the active implementation phase running upto October 31, 2026.

Campaign Metrics & Baseline Targets for Special Campaign 6:

  1. Cleanliness Campaigns: 12,208 cleanliness and outstation office drives scheduled across organizational units.
  2. Pendency & Grievance Redressal Targets: Active resolution tracking is underway for 4 MP references, 2 Parliamentary Assurances, 1 Inter-Ministerial Cabinet proposal, 58 State Government references, 2 PMO references, 72 Public Grievances (CPGRAMS), 18 Public Grievance Appeals, and 20 Easing of Rules/Process items.
  3. Record Management: Review of 2,716 physical files and 20 e-files to optimize workspace and streamline documentation.
  4. Scientific E-Waste Management: Systematic disposal targeting an aggregate of 1,011 quantities of obsolete equipment - including 602 units of IT & telecommunication equipment, 196 consumer electrical/electronic & photovoltaic units, 53 large/small electrical appliances, 5 laboratory instruments, 154 other electronic assets, and electrical tools, through MoEFCC - empanelled recyclers.

Key Focus Areas:

  1. Scientific E-Waste Management: Safe segregation and disposal, compliant with E-Waste Management Rules.
  2. Pendency Liquidation: Swift closure of public grievances, parliamentary assurances, and official references.
  3. Space Optimization: Promoting clean, clutter-free working environments through systematic record reviews and scrap clearance.

The Department remains committed to institutionalizing Swachhata and elevating governance standards throughout this month-long nationwide initiative. Daily progress updates and best practices will be shared via the national SCDPM portal.

2318072.title: APEDA Facilitates FPO-led Export of Frozen Food Products from Haryana to Canada
2318072.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
APEDA Facilitates FPO-led Export of Frozen Food Products from Haryana to Canada
Export-led Market Access Creates New Opportunities for Farmers and Food Producers
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 11:54AM by PIB Delhi

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a consignment of 24 MT of frozen food products from Sonipat, Haryana to Canada on 1st October 2026. The shipment, exported by Aterna Foods Producer Company Limited, comprises 2,295 boxes of frozen food products with a total shipment value of CAD 35,140.

The FPO-led export includes green peas, mixed vegetables, peas and carrots, sweet corn, samosa, among other products. The exporting unit was supported by APEDA under its Financial Assistance Scheme. The shipment marks another step towards expanding international market opportunities for Indian processed food products and connecting Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) with global buyers and markets.

The export highlights the growing role of Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) in developing export-oriented value chains and enabling farmers to access international markets. APEDA has been facilitating linkages between FPOs/FPCs and exporters through initiatives aimed at strengthening market access and connecting farmer groups with export opportunities. By linking agricultural produce with processing and international markets, the FPO-led model can support improved returns for producers and strengthen the participation of farmer groups in the export value chain.

Addressing the gathering, Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev congratulated the exporter and stakeholders, noting that the direct export by the FPO would significantly enhance value realisation for the producers. He also acknowledged NIFTEM’s valuable contribution and expressed optimism about expanding exports to the Canadian market.

APEDA, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, continues to facilitate market linkages and export opportunities for Indian agricultural and processed food products while supporting the integration of farmer groups into global value chains.

2318053.title: Government Extends Operational Timelines of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) Intervention to Support Exporters Amid West Asia Logistics Disruptions
2318053.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Government Extends Operational Timelines of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) Intervention to Support Exporters Amid West Asia Logistics Disruptions
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 11:01AM by PIB Delhi

In view of the continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and its impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions, the Department of Commerce has vide Notification No.37/2026-27 dated 30th September 2026 extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF – Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM).

Component II of the RELIEF scheme encourages exporters to obtain ECGC cover for upcoming shipments to the specified regions, with 95% risk coverage. The component is available for Stand Alone Policies or Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after 16 March 2026. The types of cargo covered under the benefits include Full Container Load (FCL), Less than Container Load (LCL), and Reefer containers (excluding energy shipments). Further, this component of RELIEF ensures that the premium paid by exporters shall not be increased beyond the pre-disruption level for the eligible period.

RELIEF was launched on 19 March 2026 as a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters affected by extraordinary freight escalation, heightened insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and wider West Asia maritime corridor.

The above extension reflects Government of India’s commitment to ensure export resilience, sustaining trade flows and supporting exporters amid the prevailing geopolitical and logistics uncertainties.

2318052.title: Government Extends Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products ( RoDTEP) Scheme upto 31st December 2026
2318052.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Government Extends Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products ( RoDTEP) Scheme upto 31st December 2026
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Commerce, has vide Notification No. 41/2026-27 dated 30th September 2026 extended the continuation of Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme upto 31st December 2026  and shall be available for exports made by Domestic Tariff Area  (DTAs) Units, Advance Authorisation (AA) Holders, Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Units and Export Oriented Units(EOUs).

The RoDTEP Scheme refunds embedded, un-rebated Central, State and local duties, taxes and levies borne on exported products — including prior-stage cumulative indirect taxes

The existing RoDTEP rates and value caps, as notified in Appendix 4R and Appendix 4RE as applicable on 30th September 2026 shall continue unchanged during the aforesaid period.

The above measure reflects the Government's commitment to provide support to the exporters by creating a level playing field in international markets vis-à-vis competing economies.
